sentences.en: A report of the capture and torching of Sardis by the Athenians and Ionians was brought to King Darius.

sentences.en: It is said that the king's initial response to this news was to dismiss the Ionians as being of no account,
sentences.zh: 据说国王听到这个消息后的第一反应是对爱奥尼亚人不屑一顾，认为他们无足轻重，

sentences.en: since he knew full well that they had no prospect of escaping retribution for their insurgency.
sentences.zh: 因为他心知肚明，他们根本不可能逃脱因叛乱而招致的惩罚。

sentences.en: But the Athenians he did ask after, and on being told who they were, he asked for his bow, and when he had it, he fitted an arrow, which he then fired into the heavens.
sentences.zh: 但他确实打听了雅典人的情况，当得知他们是谁后，他要来了弓，拿到弓后搭上一支箭，然后将箭射向天空。

sentences.en: And even as he sent it winging through the air, so he cried,
sentences.zh: 就在他看着箭划破长空之际，他大声喊道：

sentences.en: Zeus, do not deny me the chance to punish the Athenians.
sentences.zh: 宙斯啊，请赐予我惩罚雅典人的机会。

sentences.en: Having made this appeal, he ordered one of his servants to repeat to him three times, whenever a meal was set before him,

sentences.zh: 汤姆，这出自古代历史学家希罗多德，对吧？

sentences.zh: 而希罗多德在那段文字中展现给我们的，正是波斯入侵希腊成为必然的时刻。

sentences.zh: 他们穿过爱琴海，与居住在如今土耳其爱琴海海岸线一带的其他希腊人——也就是爱奥尼亚人——会合了。

sentences.en: And they are subjects of the Persian king because, of course, they are in Asia and the Persians that they claim to the rule of Asia.
sentences.zh: 他们是波斯国王的臣民，因为理所当然地，他们在亚洲，而波斯人宣称对亚洲拥有统治权。

sentences.en: Or at least they have been subjects of the Persian king because actually they've risen in rebellion.
sentences.zh: 或者说，他们曾经是波斯国王的臣民，因为事实上他们已经发动了起义。

sentences.en: And the Athenians have been persuaded by the Ionian leader to join them in this insurrection.
sentences.zh: 雅典人被爱奥尼亚领袖说服，加入了这场叛乱。

sentences.en: And they've marched inland from the Aegean coast with the Ionians and they've attacked the great
sentences.zh: 他们与爱奥尼亚人一起从爱琴海海岸向内陆进发，袭击了伟大的

sentences.en: city of Sardis, which is the capital of the Persian governor who kind of administers the region for the great king.
sentences.zh: 萨迪斯城，那是代表伟大的国王管理该地区的波斯总督的府城。

sentences.en: And the Persian governor retreats to the Acropolis, so the kind of the upper fortress of Sardis and holds out there.
sentences.zh: 波斯总督撤退到卫城，也就是萨迪斯的高处要塞并在那里坚守。

sentences.en: The Athenians and the Ionians can't capture that, but they are able to capture the rest of the city and they torch it.
sentences.zh: 雅典人和爱奥尼亚人无法攻克那里，但他们成功攻占了城市的其余部分并将其付之一炬。

sentences.en: Everything goes up in flames, including one of the most famous buildings in the whole of the Persian empire.
sentences.zh: 一切都陷入火海，包括波斯帝国境内最著名的建筑之一。

sentences.en: And this is a temple to Kibale, the mother goddess.
sentences.zh: 这就是母神库柏勒的神庙。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.zh: 老朋友了。

sentences.zh: 绝对是老朋友。

sentences.zh: 血腥婚礼和集体阉割之类的狂热爱好者。

sentences.zh: 显而易见，这相当于有人把飞机开进双子塔。

sentences.en: I mean, this is an appalling insult, an appalling affront.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一次令人发指的侮辱，不可容忍的冒犯。

sentences.en: And there is no way that Darius, the great king, cannot respond to it.
sentences.zh: 大流士大王绝不可能对此置之不理。

sentences.en: I mean, in much the same way that George W.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像小布什

sentences.en: Bush felt that he had to respond to 9-11.
sentences.zh: 觉得自己必须对9·11作出回应一样。

sentences.en: And in this episode and the next, we will be looking at what his response was.
sentences.zh: 在本期和下一期节目中，我们将探讨他的回应是什么。

sentences.en: So it's a really gripping, I mean, extraordinary story.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个极其扣人心弦、非同寻常的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we're going to be looking at how the Persians try to suppress the Ionian revolt, how they
sentences.zh: 所以我们要看看波斯人是如何试图平息爱奥尼亚起义的，他们如何

sentences.en: send this extraordinary amphibious operation across the Aegean with orders to destroy the city of Athens and to bring its people back as slaves.
sentences.zh: 派遣这支非同寻常的两栖作战部队横渡爱琴海，奉命摧毁雅典城并将雅典人民抓去做奴隶。

sentences.en: The Persians end up landing on a plane near Athens called Marathon.
sentences.zh: 波斯人最终在雅典附近一片名为马拉松的平原登陆。

sentences.en: And then a battle is fought at Marathon.
sentences.zh: 随后爆发了马拉松战役。

sentences.en: One way or another, it is from that battle that we get the Marathon, don't we?
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们今天所说的“马拉松”正是源于那场战役，对吧？

sentences.en: What a lovely fact that is.
sentences.zh: 多么美妙的事实啊。

sentences.en: So let's begin with our protagonist, who is not a Greek, but a Persian.
sentences.zh: 让我们从我们的主角开始讲起，他不是希腊人，而是波斯人。

sentences.en: He is the great king, the king of kings.
sentences.zh: 他是大王，万王之王。

sentences.en: And he is, so Darius is by far the most powerful man on earth at this point.
sentences.zh: 此时的大流士可以说是地球上权力最大的人。

sentences.en: I mean, he is the most powerful man who has ever lived.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是史上有史以来权力最大的人。

sentences.en: I think it's no exaggeration at this point to say that.
sentences.zh: 我认为此时这样说一点也不夸张。

sentences.en: So yeah, he's got these incredible titles, great king, king of kings, king of lands.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他拥有这些无与伦比的称号：大王、万王之王、众国之王。

sentences.en: You know, he's essentially an Iranian patriot.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他本质上是一个伊朗爱国者。

sentences.en: So he describes himself in his inscriptions as being a Persian, the son of a Persian.
sentences.zh: 因此他在铭文中称自己为波斯人，波斯人之子。

sentences.en: He's very proud of that.
sentences.zh: 他为此感到非常自豪。

sentences.en: As a Persian, he is the lord of a people who essentially in the course of a single lifetime
sentences.zh: 作为一名波斯人，他是一群人的领袖，这群人基本上在短短的一生时间里

sentences.en: have gone from provincial obscurity to becoming rulers of the greatest empire that the world has ever seen.
sentences.zh: 从偏远无名一跃成为世界上有史以来最伟大帝国的统治者。

sentences.en: And under Darius, it stretches from the Aegean all the way to the Hindu Kush and the Indus.
sentences.zh: 在大流士的统治下，帝国从爱琴海一直延伸到兴都库什山脉和印度河。

sentences.en: And the man who had won the Persians, this great empire, is a man who we have already met in the rest of history this year.
sentences.zh: 而为波斯人赢得这个伟大帝国的这个人，正是我们在今年《其余的历史》中已经遇到过的人。

sentences.en: And that is Cyrus the Great, because Dominic, the Shah of Iran, as in Jimmy Carter, was a big fan of Cyrus the Great, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 那就是居鲁士大帝，因为多米尼克，伊朗国王（就像吉米·卡特时期那样）是居鲁士大帝的超级粉丝，对吧？

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: He had a party.
sentences.zh: 他办了一场派对。

sentences.en: I think a party that's occurred more than once on the rest of his history, or been covered more than once, because it was one of history's most disastrous parties.
sentences.zh: 我想这个派对在《其余的历史》中不止一次被提及或报道过，因为它堪称历史上最灾难性的派对之一。

sentences.en: So he held this huge blowout in 1971 to celebrate what they claimed was the 2500th anniversary of the founding of the Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 所以在1971年，他举办了一场盛大的狂欢，来庆祝他们所声称的波斯帝国建国2500周年。

sentences.en: What the Shah wanted to do in the 1960s and 70s was to lay claim to the heritage of Cyrus
sentences.zh: 沙阿在20世纪60和70年代想要做的是继承居鲁士的遗产，

sentences.en: and to say he is a new Cyrus building Persia up, you know, from nothing to become a genuine superpower.
sentences.zh: 并宣称他是一个新的居鲁士，将波斯从“零”开始建设成为一个真正的超级大国。

sentences.en: And Cyrus, unlike the Shah, was a really, really serious person, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 而居鲁士与沙阿不同，是一个非常、非常严肃的人，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he was the great, he was the great empire builder, arguably, in all history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是伟大的帝国缔造者，可以说是全人类历史上最伟大的。

sentences.en: The prototypical empire builder.
sentences.zh: 堪称帝国缔造者的原型。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he dies in 529 BC, but before that, he'd ruled for three decades.
sentences.zh: 对，他在公元前529年去世，但在那之前，他已经统治了三十年。

sentences.en: And over the course of that reign, he enjoys one of the greatest winning streaks in the whole of history.
sentences.zh: 在他统治期间，他迎来了整个历史上最辉煌的一连串胜利。

sentences.en: So he's up there with Alexander, Julius Caesar, one of the greats.
sentences.zh: 所以他与亚历山大大帝、尤利乌斯·凯萨齐名，是最伟大的人物之一。

sentences.en: And he topples a succession of famous and ancient empires.
sentences.zh: 他推翻了一连串著名而古老的帝国。

sentences.en: So the first empire that he topples is the Empire of the Medes.
sentences.zh: 他推翻的第一个帝国就是米底帝国。

sentences.en: And they occupy kind of northwest Iran.
sentences.zh: 他们占据了大致的伊朗西北部。

sentences.en: So Tehran would be in what was media.
sentences.zh: 所以德黑兰就位于曾经的米底境内。

sentences.en: And the Persians had been subjects to the Medes.
sentences.zh: 而波斯人曾经是米底人的臣民。

sentences.en: So the Persians actually see the Medes as cousins.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯人实际上把米底人看作表亲。

sentences.en: And when they conquer the Medes, they essentially incorporate the Medes in as kind of junior partners in the entire enterprise of running this empire.
sentences.zh: 当他们征服米底人时，基本上将米底人作为初级合伙人纳入了经营这个帝国的整个宏图伟业中。

sentences.en: And to the Greeks, the Persians and the Medes are indistinguishable.
sentences.zh: 在希腊人看来，波斯人和米底人是没有区别的。

sentences.en: They're likelier to refer to the Persians as Medes.
sentences.zh: 他们更倾向于把波斯人称为米底人。

sentences.en: So if you hear Medes in this, it's kind of Medes and Persians.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在这里听到“米底人”，其实指的就是米底人和波斯人。

sentences.en: So Cyrus, he's now got the Medes on board.
sentences.zh: 所以，居鲁士现在把米底人收编了。

sentences.en: Then he marches eastwards into what is now Turkey, so Anatolia.
sentences.zh: 接着他向东进军，进入现在的土耳其，也就是安纳托利亚。

sentences.en: And he attacks a city we've already heard of, Sardis.
sentences.zh: 他攻击了一个我们已经听说过的城市，萨迪斯。

sentences.en: And this is the capital of the Lydians.
sentences.zh: 这是吕底亚人的首都。

sentences.en: And the Lydians are a very prosperous, wealthy power.
sentences.zh: 吕底亚人是一个非常繁荣、富庶的强国。

sentences.en: They have subjected the Ionian Greeks on the Aegean shore to their rule.
sentences.zh: 他们将爱琴海沿岸的爱奥尼亚希腊人置于他们的统治之下。

sentences.en: And the source of their power is their ability to monetize their power.
sentences.zh: 他们权力的源泉在于他们将权力货币化的能力。

sentences.en: And they've literally monetized it because they've invented money.
sentences.zh: 他们确实将其货币化了，因为他们发明了货币。

sentences.en: And this is why the last king, Croesus, who gets defeated by Cyrus, overthrown by him.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么最后一位国王克罗伊索斯被居鲁士击败并推翻后，

sentences.en: You know, he's still a byword.
sentences.zh: 他仍然是一个代名词。

sentences.en: You're rich as Croesus.
sentences.zh: “富得像克罗伊索斯一样”。

sentences.en: You know, you're fabulously, fabulously rich.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，富可敌国，极其富有。

sentences.en: So now the Lydians have been toppled.
sentences.zh: 现在吕底亚人已经被推翻了。

sentences.en: And with the defeat of the Lydians, the Ionians also come under the rule of the Persians.
sentences.zh: 随着吕底亚人的战败，爱奥尼亚人也落入了波斯人的统治之下。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just to remind people, this is modern-day Turkey, basically, that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 顺便提醒大家一下，我们讨论的基本上就是当今的土耳其。

sentences.en: That's Anatolia is now subject to the Persians, as well as media.
sentences.zh: 安纳托利亚以及米底现在都臣服于波斯人了。

sentences.en: And this leaves perhaps the greatest power of all to be conquered.
sentences.zh: 这使得也许最强大的帝国成为了下一个被征服的目标。

sentences.en: And this is Babylon.
sentences.zh: 这就是巴比伦。

sentences.en: You know, this fabulous ancient city, the richest city in the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这座神话般的古城，世界上最富有的城市。

sentences.en: And Cyrus conquers that in 539.
sentences.zh: 居鲁士在公元前539年征服了它。

sentences.en: And Herodotus gives a brilliant estimation of just how vast Babylon was.
sentences.zh: 希罗多德对巴比伦的浩瀚规模做出了极高明的估计。

sentences.en: He writes, according to local tradition, such was the size of the city that those who lived
sentences.zh: 他写道，根据当地传统，这座城市的规模如此之大，以至于居住

sentences.en: in the center of Babylon had no idea when the Persians broke into the city that the suburbs had fallen, for it was a time of festival and all were dancing and indulging themselves
sentences.zh: 在巴比伦中心的人们，在波斯人攻入城中时根本不知道郊区已经沦陷，因为当时正值节日，所有人都沉浸在载歌载舞和纵情

sentences.en: in pleasures.
sentences.zh: 享乐之中。

sentences.en: And for Cyrus, the conquest of Babylon is what sets the seal on his ascent to greatness.
sentences.zh: 对居鲁士而言，征服巴比伦是他登上伟大巅峰的最后印记。

sentences.en: So there's a slightly kind of Trumpian quality to his boasting of his inscriptions.
sentences.zh: 所以他在铭文中的吹嘘带有一点川普式的特质。

sentences.en: He proclaims, every king on earth brought me heavy tribute and kissed my feet where I sat in Babylon.
sentences.zh: 他宣告：世上每一个国王都向我进贡沉重的贡品，并在我坐镇巴比伦时亲吻我的双脚。

sentences.en: So he's made it.
sentences.zh: 所以他成功了。

sentences.en: So to give people just a sense, just if you think about looking at the map, we are talking about an empire that started in modern-day Iran and that has swallowed up Iraq, which
sentences.zh: 为了给听众一个概念，如果你看一下地图，我们所说的是一个始于现代伊朗、吞并了伊拉克的帝国，

sentences.en: is where Babylon effectively was.
sentences.zh: 伊拉克正是巴比伦的所在地。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: And Anatolia, which is sort of inland Turkey.
sentences.zh: 还有安纳托利亚，也就是土耳其内地。

sentences.en: Turkey, and has also taken the Turkish coast, which is inhabited by Greek speakers.
sentences.zh: 土耳其，并且还占领了说希腊语的人所居住的土耳其海岸。

sentences.en: So it is a vast empire.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个庞大的帝国。

sentences.en: And also has conquered what would now be Syria and Israel and Lebanon because they were subject to Babylon.
sentences.zh: 并且还征服了现在的叙利亚、以色列和黎巴嫩，因为它们原本就臣服于巴比伦。

sentences.en: So they come under Cyrus's rule.
sentences.zh: 所以它们也落入了居鲁士的统治之下。

sentences.en: And indeed is eyeing up Egypt, am I right?
sentences.zh: 而且事实上正对准了埃及，我没说错吧？

sentences.en: So Cyrus doesn't attack Egypt.
sentences.zh: 居鲁士并没有进攻埃及。

sentences.en: He goes off into Central Asia and that's where he reaches the Indus.
sentences.zh: 他去了中亚，并在那里一直到达了印度河。

sentences.en: He reaches the Hindu Kush.
sentences.zh: 他到达了兴都库什山脉。

sentences.en: He goes even further and that's where he's killed.
sentences.zh: 他走得更远，最后就是在那里阵亡的。

sentences.en: His son has eyes up Egypt, Cambyses, right?
sentences.zh: 他的儿子盯上了埃及，对吧，冈比西斯？

sentences.en: His son, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是他的儿子。

sentences.en: So when Cyrus dies fighting in Central Asia in 529, he leaves behind him two sons.
sentences.zh: 所以当居鲁士于公元前529年在中亚作战阵亡时，他留下了两个儿子。

sentences.en: And the first of these you just mentioned, Cambyses, he becomes the new king of kings.
sentences.zh: 其中的第一个就是你刚才提到的冈比西斯，他成为了新的万王之王。

sentences.en: But Cyrus also has a younger son called Bardia and Bardia is entrusted with the rule of the eastern satrapies, the eastern provinces as they're called.
sentences.zh: 但居鲁士还有一个小儿子叫巴尔迪亚，巴尔迪亚被委任统治东方的总督区，也就是人们所说的东方行省。

sentences.en: And it's obvious that Cyrus is very keen to ensure that the rule of the world remains within the family.
sentences.zh: 显然，居鲁士非常渴望确保对世界的统治权始终留在家族内部。

sentences.en: So to ensure that kind of rival nobles can't get in on the act, Cambyses has married both his sisters.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了确保那些贵族对头无法插手，冈比西斯娶了自己的两个亲妹妹。

sentences.en: And this is an unprecedented display of inceSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一场前所未有的乱伦展示。

sentences.en: It's not, there's nothing in Persian custom that would license that.
sentences.zh: 不是的，波斯习俗中没有任何东西能为此提供正当理由。

sentences.en: But Cyrus, Cambyses, Bardia, you know, they want it to remain a kind of family concern.
sentences.zh: 但居鲁士、冈比西斯、巴尔迪亚，你知道的，他们希望这能保持为一种家族内部事务。

sentences.en: And this is obviously bad news for even distant cousins of the Persian royal family.
sentences.zh: 对于波斯王室甚至那些远房表亲来说，这显然都不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: And one of these distant cousins is Darius, who, when Cambyses becomes king, is still in his 20s.
sentences.zh: 而这些远房表亲之一就是大流士，当冈比西斯成为国王时，大流士还处于二十多岁的年纪。

sentences.en: And he is the lance bearer to Cambyses, which might sound a slightly menial function, but
sentences.zh: 他是冈比西斯的持矛卫士，这听起来可能有点像是个卑微的职务，但是

sentences.en: it doesn't because it indicates that essentially he's playing the role of a personal bodyguard
sentences.zh: 其实不然，因为这表明他本质上扮演着私人保镖的角色，

sentences.en: and proximity to the to the monarch in Persia is a kind of indicator of status.
sentences.zh: 而且在波斯，与君主的亲疏程度是地位的一种指标。

sentences.en: So actually, it's a very kind of splendid honorific.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这是一个非常光彩的荣誉头衔。

sentences.en: I mean, it marks you out as certainly a kind of major player at court, even if you're not a royal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对标明你是朝廷中的一个重要人物，即使你并非王室成员。

sentences.en: And it enables Darius clearly to be privy to very, very sensitive royal secrets.
sentences.zh: 这显然使大流士能够接触到非常非常机密的王室秘密。

sentences.en: He's got his finger on the pulse.
sentences.zh: 他消息极其灵通。

sentences.en: He knows what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他对外面的事情了如指掌。

sentences.en: And that is what enables him in the summer of 522, when the dynasty of Cyrus abruptly implodes to have a very good idea of what is going on and to know how to respond.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，在公元前522年的夏天，当居鲁士的王朝突然崩溃时，他能够对局势有很好的把握并且知道该如何应对。

sentences.en: So the account that we have comes from Darius himself, and how much of it is true is impossible to say.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们拥有的记载来自大流士本人，至于其中有多少是真实的，根本无法判定。

sentences.en: But it basically begins with Cambyses going mad, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但故事基本上是从冈比西斯发疯开始的，对吧？

sentences.en: He goes mad and he becomes incredibly jealous of Bardia and has him put to death.
sentences.zh: 他疯了，对巴尔迪亚嫉妒得发狂，并下令将他处死。

sentences.en: So far, so standard kind of Game of Thrones style was the Roses fraternal jealousy.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，这还算标准的《权力的游戏》或《玫瑰战争》风格的手足相残式的嫉妒。

sentences.en: But now there's a tremendous twist, which I'm looking forward to hearing you explain.
sentences.zh: 但现在出现了一个巨大的反转，我很期待听你来解释。

sentences.en: So tell us what happens next.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我们接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: So Bardia has been killed on the orders of Cambyses, who is still kind of whooping it up in Egypt, which he's just conquered.
sentences.zh: 因此，巴尔迪亚是在冈比西斯的命令下被杀的，而冈比西斯当时还在他刚征服的埃及得意洋洋地寻欢作乐。

sentences.en: The twist is that Bardia is now replaced in the eastern provinces by someone who looks exactly like Bardia, but isn't.
sentences.zh: 这个反转就是，东方行省的巴尔迪亚现在被另一个人取代了，那个人长得跟巴尔迪亚一模一样，但根本不是他。

sentences.en: So the Magi are the kind of the Persian equivalent of the Brahmins.
sentences.zh: 所以“玛哥斯”有点像是波斯版的婆罗门。

sentences.en: They're like a kind of priestly caste.
sentences.zh: 他们类似于一种祭司阶层。

sentences.en: And this kind of fake Magus, I mean, by amazing coincidence, he's exactly resembles Bardia.
sentences.zh: 而这个假玛哥斯，我的意思是，由于惊人的巧合，他长得跟巴尔迪亚一模一样。

sentences.en: And this fake Bardia then stages a rebellion against Cambyses.
sentences.zh: 于是这个假巴尔迪亚便发动了针对冈比西斯的叛乱。

sentences.en: The news is brought to Cambyses in Egypt.
sentences.zh: 这个消息传到了身在埃及的冈比西斯耳中。

sentences.en: He's furious, of course.
sentences.zh: 他当然勃然大怒。

sentences.en: He leaps on his horse, leads an expedition out of Egypt through Syria.
sentences.zh: 他翻身上马，率领一支远征军从埃及出发，穿过叙利亚。

sentences.en: And in Syria, he pauses, has some food, and then he's climbing up onto his horse.
sentences.zh: 在叙利亚，他停下来吃点东西，然后正准备爬上马背。

sentences.en: And his sword accidentally slips.
sentences.zh: 结果他的剑不小心滑落了。

sentences.en: And he stabs himself in the thigh with it.
sentences.zh: 他用剑刺伤了自己的大腿。

sentences.en: And this wound then goes septic.
sentences.zh: 随后这个伤口开始化脓感染。

sentences.en: And he dies very shortly afterwards.
sentences.zh: 不久之后他就去世了。

sentences.en: So that's Cambyses out of the way.
sentences.zh: 好了，这样冈比西斯就被排除在外了。

sentences.en: And at this point, the false Magus, the kind of the pretend Bardia, declares that he is now king of kings.
sentences.zh: 就在此时，那个假的玛哥斯，也就是假巴尔迪亚，宣称自己现在是万王之王。

sentences.en: And the only people who know the truth that this isn't really Bardia is Darius and six southern noblemen, and they get together a posse, and they gallop from Syria across the
sentences.zh: 唯一知道真相——即这不是真正的巴尔迪亚——的人只有大流士和另外六名南方贵族，他们召集了一支队伍，从叙利亚策马狂奔，穿过美索不达米亚干旱开阔的平原，

sentences.en: kind of the parched flatlands of Mesopotamia, up the Corazon Highway, which is the road that sneaks up through the Zagros Mountains up towards the great plateau of Iran.
sentences.zh: 沿着呼罗珊公路北上，这条路穿过扎格罗斯山脉，一直通往伊朗高原。

sentences.en: And they arrive at a place called Sikia Vautish, which is up in the heights of the Zagros Mountains, surrounded by rich fields.
sentences.zh: 他们抵达了一个叫作西基亚·沃蒂什的地方，它位于扎格罗斯山脉的高处，周围环绕着肥沃的田野。

sentences.en: There are famous horses from these fields.
sentences.zh: 这些田野里出产著名的骏马。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of beautiful spot.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一个非常美丽的地方。

sentences.en: And Bardia is, or rather the fake Bardia, is hanging out there enjoying his concubines when Darius, the six other noblemen, and the kind of posse of men they've brought burst in
sentences.zh: 当时巴尔迪亚，或者说假巴尔迪亚，正待在那里享受着他的姬妾们的陪伴，这时大流士、另外六名贵族以及他们带来的随从队伍突然闯了进来，

sentences.en: on him, take the fake Bardia completely by surprise.
sentences.zh: 打了他一个措手不及。

sentences.en: He reaches for a chair, smashes it up, tries to use the chair leg to fend them off.
sentences.zh: 他伸手去抓一把椅子，把它砸碎，试图用椅腿来抵挡他们。

sentences.en: It's no good.
sentences.zh: 但这没有用。

sentences.en: He is dispatched.
sentences.zh: 他被处决了。

sentences.en: And Darius then proclaims to the world that there's, you know, there's been this terrible scam, that Bardia had been replaced by this false magus, and that he is now the king.
sentences.zh: 随后大流士向全世界宣告，发生了一场可怕的骗局，巴尔迪亚被这个假玛哥斯取而代之了，而现在他才是国王。

sentences.en: Quite deep waters, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这里面水很深。

sentences.en: Quite a lot of improbabilities there.
sentences.zh: 里面有相当多的不可思议之处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You don't have to be a tremendous skeptic to think that actually what was happening was that he had planned a coup himself, and he organizes the murder of these two brothers,
sentences.zh: 你不需要是个极度多疑的人，也会觉得实际情况其实是他自己策划了一场政变，并且一手安排了这两个兄弟的谋杀，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, because I think the sword in the thigh accident.
sentences.zh: 对，因为我觉得大腿中剑的意外……

sentences.en: Come on, that's, yeah.
sentences.zh: 拜托，这太假了。

sentences.en: He accidentally, what is it?
sentences.zh: 他怎么个意外法？

sentences.en: He accidentally stabbed yourself in the thigh with it.
sentences.zh: 他怎么就意外地用剑刺中了自己的大腿呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, and even that's not as improbable as the idea that, you know, there's a guy who looks exactly like the murdered king.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且甚至这都不如这种说法来得荒谬：有一个人长得和被谋杀的国王一模一样。

sentences.en: So I think the likelihood is there isn't a false Bardia, there isn't a kind of Maegian doppelganger, and that the person who gets killed by Darius and his fellow conspirators
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得很有可能根本没有假巴尔迪亚，也没有什么玛哥斯替身，大流士和他的同谋者在西基亚·沃蒂什杀死的

sentences.en: in Sekia Vautish was actually Bardia himself.
sentences.zh: 其实就是巴尔迪亚本人。

sentences.en: And there's very good corroborating evidence for this, because the moment Darius announces
sentences.zh: 而且有非常充分的佐证来支持这一点，因为就在大流士宣布自己登基的瞬间，接二连三的叛乱爆发了，这些叛乱发生在波斯本土、

sentences.en: his accession to the throne, there is a succession of rebellions, and these take place in Persia
sentences.zh: 北部的米底，以及位于伊朗西南部的埃兰。

sentences.en: itself, in Media, just to the north, and in Elam, which is a country in the southwest of Iran.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这些都是帝国最核心的腹地。

sentences.en: So basically, these are the absolute heartlands of the empire.
sentences.zh: 这些可以说是伊朗人的大本营。

sentences.en: These are the kind of, you know, the Iranian strongholds.
sentences.zh: 显然，在这些伊朗本土势力看来，大流士是一个非法的国王。

sentences.en: And clearly, in these Iranian strongholds, they are viewing Darius as an illegitimate king.
sentences.zh: 他花了两年时间进行绝望的战斗才镇压了这些叛乱。

sentences.en: And it takes him two years of desperate fighting to crush these rebellions.
sentences.zh: 即使在他平定之后，叛乱的星星之火仍然不断燃起。

sentences.en: And even once he's done it, the kind of the bushfires of insurrection keep kind of blazing.
sentences.zh: 他花了很长时间才让所有这些叛乱稳定下来并被安抚。

sentences.en: It takes him a long, long time to stabilize and pacify all these kind of rebellions.
sentences.zh: 他之所以能做到这一点，部分原因在于他是一个残暴冷酷的人，对吧？

sentences.en: And he does it partly because he's a brutal and ruthless man, right?
sentences.zh: 他做了必须要做的事。

sentences.en: He does what needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 用我们最喜欢的话来说，他是个狠角色。

sentences.en: You know, he's a serious person, to use our favorite terminology.
sentences.zh: 是的，你敢惹大流士，他就会杀了你，而且会用极其恐怖的方式杀死你。

sentences.en: Yes, you mess with Darius and he will kill you, and he will kill you very horribly.
sentences.zh: 因此，大流士统治的叛乱者们都被处以了极具震慑力的可怕暴力。

sentences.en: So the rebels against Darius's rule are dispatched with very salutary displays of hideous violence.
sentences.zh: 在波斯，那些叛乱的贵族被高高地串在无边无际的木桩森林上。

sentences.en: So in Persia, the rebellious aristocrats there are impaled on an immense forest of stakes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，绵延数英里之遥。

sentences.en: I mean, kind of spreading for miles and miles.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些木桩放置的地方，正是1971年伊朗国王举办派对的那个地方。

sentences.en: And actually, these stakes were placed on the very place where the Shah of Iran in 1971 would hold his party.
sentences.zh: 我想伊朗国王当时可能并没有重点关注这一点。

sentences.en: And I think that's something that perhaps the Shah of Iran didn't major on.
sentences.zh: 没有关注他来自马克西姆餐厅的鱼子酱什么的。

sentences.en: With his caviar from Maxim's or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有安妮公主。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Princess Anne.
sentences.zh: 安妮公主，没错。

sentences.en: Princess Anne, yeah.
sentences.zh: 不过说句公道话，她可不会对人手软。

sentences.en: She wouldn't take any prisoners, though, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 我想她绝对会把叛乱者串在木桩上的。

sentences.en: She definitely impaled rebels, I think.
sentences.zh: 她绝对会的。

sentences.en: She absolutely would.
sentences.zh: 那另一个人呢，那个来自米底的人？

sentences.en: And what about this other guy, this guy from Media?
sentences.zh: 米底人也推出了他们自己的僭主，对吧？

sentences.en: So the Medes come up with a pretender of their own, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他的下场可一点也不美妙。

sentences.en: And he doesn't come to a very happy end at all.
sentences.zh: 米底的伟大首都埃克巴塔纳，据希罗多德所说，有点像米那斯提力斯。

sentences.en: So the great capital of Media is this place called Ectana, which, according to Herodotus, is a bit like Minas Tirith.
sentences.zh: 它是由围绕着核心要塞的一圈圈防御工事构成的。

sentences.en: It's kind of rings of fortifications around a central stronghold.
sentences.zh: 每一道墙都有着美丽而不同的颜色。

sentences.en: And each wall is a beautiful, different color.
sentences.zh: 这位米底贵族就是在那里自立为王，成了一个独立国王。

sentences.en: And this is where this Median aristocrat has set himself up as a kind of independent king.
sentences.zh: 大流士俘虏了他，割掉了他的鼻子、舌头和耳朵。

sentences.en: Darius captures him, has his nose cut off, his tongue, his ears.
sentences.zh: 然后弄瞎他的一只眼睛，好让他亲眼目睹所有支持他的人都在他周围被串在木桩上。

sentences.en: He's then blinded in one eye so that he can witness all his supporters being impaled around him.
sentences.zh: 接着把他锁在埃克巴塔纳的城门前，让所有人都能看到他。

sentences.en: He's then chained before the gates of Ectana, where everyone could see him.
sentences.zh: 当然最后，他也难逃被串在木桩上的命运。

sentences.en: And then, of course, he too is impaled.
sentences.zh: 被串在木桩上是一种极其痛苦的死法。

sentences.en: And to be impaled is a really hideous death.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这可能要持续好几天，尖锐的木桩刺入你的内脏。

sentences.en: I mean, it can take days, sharp spike into your bowels.
sentences.zh: 一个技艺高超的行刑手会以这样一种方式将你串起来：既不刺破你的任何重要器官，

sentences.en: A very skilled impaler will impale you in such a way that none of your vital organs are pierced,
sentences.zh: 让你就那样坐在那里，一连几个小时甚至几天，任由人们围观指点。

sentences.en: so that you just sort of sit there, as it were, for hours or days at a time where people came and looked at you.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我认为这是一种可怕的死法。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's a terrible way to die, frankly.
sentences.zh: 是的，波斯人是折磨人致死的大师。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the Persians are masters of the protracted death.
sentences.zh: 他们还有一种可怕的刑罚，就是把一个浑身涂满蜂蜜的家伙关在一个

sentences.en: So they also have a hideous one where they kind of lock a bloke who's been covered in honey inside her,
sentences.zh: 两端扣合的独木舟里，只把手和脚露在外面。

sentences.en: you know, with the hands and the feet sticking out of two barges that have been placed over him.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他就会被蛆虫吃掉，苍蝇也会在他的眼睛里产卵。

sentences.en: And basically, he just gets, you know, you get eaten by maggots and flies, lay eggs in your eyes.
sentences.zh: 我的天，简直太可怕太可怕了。

sentences.en: And I mean, just horrible, horrible.
sentences.zh: 时代不同了。

sentences.en: Different times.
sentences.zh: 咱们面对现实吧。

sentences.en: Let's face it.
sentences.zh: 大流士在做必须要做的事。

sentences.en: Darius is doing what has to be done.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这种做法会赢得桑德布鲁克政治立场的尊重。

sentences.en: It's the kind of thing I think that would garner respect from the Sandbrook political position.
sentences.zh: 我正想说呢，我尊重这一点。

sentences.en: I was about to say, I respect it.
sentences.zh: 我不一定赞同，但我尊重。

sentences.en: I don't necessarily approve it, but I respect it.
sentences.zh: 我懂你的行事方式和手段。

sentences.en: I know your ways and means.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯人的叛乱被平息了。

sentences.en: So that's the Persians crushed.
sentences.zh: 米底叛军也被平息了。

sentences.en: The Median rebels crushed.
sentences.zh: 但还有埃兰人。

sentences.en: There are still the Elamites.
sentences.zh: 埃兰人的叛乱是一段极其晦涩的历史时期。

sentences.en: And what is, I mean, it's an incredibly obscure period of history, the Elamite rebellion.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，它其实是世界历史上最具创新性的事件之一。

sentences.en: But I would argue that it's actually one of the most innovative episodes in world history.
sentences.zh: 它使大流士成为一个极具影响力的君王，几乎可以与君士坦丁或伟大伊斯兰哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克相提并论。

sentences.en: And it marks Darius out as a very consequential king, kind of almost up there with Constantine or Abdul Malik, the great Islamic caliph.
sentences.zh: 因为埃兰人不断叛乱。

sentences.en: Because the Elamites keep rebelling.
sentences.zh: 大流士不断镇压他们，而他们又再次叛乱。

sentences.en: Darius keeps crushing them and they keep rebelling again.
sentences.zh: 因此，他所做的是将一种极其独特的波斯超自然观武器化。

sentences.en: And so what he does is to weaponize a very distinctively Persian understanding of the supernatural.
sentences.zh: 因为波斯人与当时近东地区的绝大多数人不同。

sentences.en: Because the Persians, they're not like most other people in the Near East at this time.
sentences.zh: 因为他们基本上将整个宇宙道德化了。

sentences.en: Because they have essentially moralized the entire universe.
sentences.zh: 他们认为宇宙受控于一场永恒的宇宙战争，一方是他们称之为“阿尔塔”（Arta）的真理，另一方是他们称之为“德劳加”（Drauga）的普遍谎言。

sentences.en: They see the universe as being governed by a perpetual cosmic war between truth, which they call Arta, and the lie, this universal lie, which they call Drauga.
sentences.zh: 大流士把自己塑造为“阿尔塔”的代理人，“阿尔塔”既意味着秩序，也意味着真理。

sentences.en: And Darius casts himself as the agent of Arta, which means order as well as truth.
sentences.zh: 对于波斯人来说，秩序和真理是同义词。

sentences.en: To the Persians, order and truth are kind of synonymous.
sentences.zh: 它们是同一回事。

sentences.en: They're the same thing.
sentences.zh: 他的天才之处在于将他的敌人打上“德劳加”（即谎言）代理人的烙印。

sentences.en: And his genius is to brand his enemies as agents of Drauga, of the lie.
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，是将他们视为“得麦瓦”（Daevas）的代理人，这些是某种恶魔或假神。

sentences.en: And more specifically, as agents of Daevas, who are kind of demons, false gods.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么大流士谴责假巴尔迪亚是一个“说谎的国王”。

sentences.en: And this is why Darius had condemned the false Bardia as a liar king.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是一个说过谎话的人。

sentences.en: He is not just someone who had been telling fibs.
sentences.zh: 他是一个与宇宙中最黑暗、最恶毒的力量勾结在一起的人。

sentences.en: He's someone who has been in hock to all that is darkest and most malign in the cosmos.
sentences.zh: 因此，在公元前520年，当埃兰人发动又一次叛乱时——我觉得我有点记不清了，

sentences.en: So in 520, when the Elamites launch yet another rebellion, I think I'm losing track slightly.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是他们的第三次或第四次叛乱了——

sentences.en: I think maybe it's their third or fourth.
sentences.zh: 大流士采取了这极其重大的一步。

sentences.en: Darius takes this really, really momentous step.
sentences.zh: 他告诉他的军队——这在历史上是前所未闻的——如果他们与埃兰人作战，他们可以期待——我引用原话——“神圣的赐福”，

sentences.en: He tells his army, and no one had ever done this before in history, that if they go to war against the Elamites, they can expect, and I quote, divine blessings,
sentences.zh: 无论是在生前还是死后。

sentences.en: both in their lives and after death.
sentences.zh: 这样做的原因是埃兰人——我引用原话——“不忠”。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is because the Elamites are, and I quote, faithless.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅冒犯了大流士本人，还冒犯了宇宙的真理与秩序，以及光与真理之神阿胡拉·马兹达，这位神明正是真理的主宰。

sentences.en: They are offenders, not just against Darius himself, but against the truth and order of the cosmos and of the God of light and truth, Ahura Mazda, who is the God of this truth.
sentences.zh: 怎么强调这有多疯狂都不为过，因为在那个时期，没有人真正认为一个不崇拜某神的人应该因为

sentences.en: And it's hard to overemphasize how mad this is, because at this period, no one had really thought that a people who neglect the worship of a God should be kind of punished for,
sentences.zh: 那不是他们的神而受到惩罚。

sentences.en: you know, it's not their God.
sentences.zh: 这根本不重要。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要崇拜它？

sentences.en: Why would they be worshiping it?
sentences.zh: 但大流士正在确立这样一种观念：即使埃兰人未必崇拜阿胡拉·马兹达，他们仍然应该为此受到惩罚。

sentences.en: But Darius is kind of instituting this notion that even though the Elamites don't necessarily worship Ahura Mazda, they should still be punished for it.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，这是一个非常重大的创新，因为它包含了某些相当激进观念的种子，这些观念将在后世产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: And you can see there that this is a really, really portentous innovation, because it contains the seeds of some quite radical notions, which will have a very long afterlife.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这种观念认为外国叛军可以被谴责为反叛他们所不崇拜的神，战士们不仅可以被许诺此生的财富，

sentences.en: So basically, the idea that foreign rebels can be condemned as rebels against a God that they don't worship, that warriors can be promised not just riches in this life, but,
sentences.zh: 还可以被许诺天堂里的各种好处。

sentences.en: you know, all kinds of benefits in paradise.
sentences.zh: 以神明或某种道德真理、秩序的名义进行的征服，可以被塑造成一种神圣的道德责任。

sentences.en: And that conquest in the name of a God or of a kind of moral truth or order can be cast as a moral duty.
sentences.zh: 以神明或某种道德真理、秩序的名义进行的征服，可以被塑造成一种神圣的道德责任。

sentences.en: And these are, you know, these are going to, these are going to have a very, very long life.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，这些东西将会拥有非常、非常漫长的生命力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Ideas that have never gone away, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那些从未消逝过的理念，汤姆。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: So it's, it's, I think, a very kind of crucial moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，这是一个非常关键的时刻。

sentences.en: And it helps Darius secure his rule, crush his enemies,
sentences.zh: 这有助于大流士巩固统治、粉碎敌人，

sentences.en: this combination of kind of militant devotion to notions of truth and a readiness to impale people and kind of mutilate them.
sentences.zh: 这种结合了对真理观念的狂热忠诚，以及随时准备将人穿刺并施以肢解的作风。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, it's a great combination, very effective.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这组合绝了，非常有效。

sentences.en: And it helps him to set the Persian Empire on foundations that are so secure that it will endure pretty much in a state of peace.
sentences.zh: 这有助于他为波斯帝国奠定极其稳固的基础，使其能够在一个相当和平的状态下延续下去。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, give or take the old rebellion or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，除了一些偶尔发生的叛乱之类的。

sentences.en: For about two centuries until it ends up conquered by Alexander.
sentences.zh: 大约持续两个世纪，直到最终被亚历山大征服。

sentences.en: And he's not just, I mean, he's not just fearsome and he's not just good at weaponizing religion.
sentences.zh: 而且他不只是——我的意思是，他不只是令人畏惧，他不只是擅长将宗教武器化。

sentences.en: I mean, he's also just very good at running empires, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他也很擅长治理帝国，对吧？

sentences.en: He, he, he does, he, he does what needs to be done.
sentences.zh: 他确实在做那些需要做的事。

sentences.en: He, the administrative legwork, you know, he gets up and he does his paperwork, basically.
sentences.zh: 行政方面的杂务，你知道的，他Basically就是起床处理文件。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we've compared him to Constantine, but you could also compare him to Augustus.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把他比作君士坦丁，但你也可以把他比作奥古斯都。

sentences.en: I mean, he's, he's, he's that significant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他就是如此重要。

sentences.en: He's that able.
sentences.zh: 他就是这么有能力。

sentences.en: And he found this great palace to serve him as his nerve center, as his powerhouse, and also as the showcase for his power.
sentences.zh: 他建立了一座宏伟的宫殿，作为他的神经中枢、权力核心，同时也作为他权力的展示橱窗。

sentences.en: And the Persians call it Parsa, so basically Persia, and the Greeks will call it Persepolis.
sentences.zh: 波斯人称之为帕尔萨，也就是波斯，而希腊人则称之为波斯波利斯。

sentences.en: And this is the site where the Persian rebels had been impaled.
sentences.zh: 这就是波斯叛军被穿刺示众的地方。

sentences.en: You know, this is where the Shah and Ducos will have his great party.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这也是沙阿和杜科斯将举办盛大派对的地方。

sentences.en: And Persepolis becomes the, the kind of the focus of an immense network of precisely organized tribute that spans the entire empire.
sentences.zh: 而波斯波利斯成为了一个极其精准组织的贡赋网络的核心，这个网络横跨整个帝国。

sentences.en: And Cyrus and Cambyses, they hadn't really been bothered with this kind of thing, but Darius is, you know, he has the brain of an accountant.
sentences.zh: 居鲁士和冈比西斯其实并不太在意这种事，但大流士，你知道的，他有着会计师的大脑。

sentences.en: And actually the Persian nobles mock him behind his back as a shopkeeper, but it is precisely this mastery of tribute and of fiscal policy and so on.
sentences.zh: 事实上，波斯贵族在背后嘲笑他是店小二，但恰恰是这种对贡赋、财政政策等的掌控力，

sentences.en: That actually is at least as important as his, his talents as a general, you know,
sentences.zh: 实际上至少和他作为将领的才能一样重要，你知道的，

sentences.en: it's a combination of knowing how to conquer people and then knowing how to screw the money out of them so that they don't rebel.
sentences.zh: 这就是懂得如何征服人们，然后懂得如何榨干他们的钱财以免他们叛乱的结合。

sentences.en: But the real genius is that he allies that with this sort of moral ideological vision, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但真正的天才在于，他将这一点与这种道德意识形态愿景结合起来了，不是吗？

sentences.en: That you basically combine somebody who's brilliant at actually extracting money from people and who's,
sentences.zh: 基本上就是将一个极擅长从人们身上榨取钱财的人，一个实用主义的帝国缔造者，

sentences.en: you're a great practical empire builder with somebody who creates an ideological justification for empire, where his empire is a reflection of divine order.
sentences.zh: 与一个为帝国创造意识形态正当性的人结合起来，在那里，他的帝国是神圣秩序的反映。

sentences.en: And to challenge it makes you a rebel against harmony and order and truth and all that is, you know, divinely sanctioned and all that is good in this world.
sentences.zh: 而挑战它就使你成为一个背叛和谐、秩序、真理以及世间所有神圣庇佑和美好事物的人。

sentences.en: You know, so, so you get conquered by the Persians, you get told, you've got to give enormous amounts of tribute.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当你被波斯人征服时，你会被告知，你必须交纳巨额贡赋。

sentences.en: And then you get told that if you're going to rebel, then, you know, you're, you're,
sentences.zh: 然后你会听到，如果你要反叛，那么，你知道的，你就是在，

sentences.en: you're in rebellion against truth and order and that this truth and order spans the entire cosmos.
sentences.zh: 你是在背叛真理与秩序，而这种真理与秩序横跨整个宇宙。

sentences.en: And so it enables Darius, who I think is, is clearly not a very pleasant man to cast himself as a kind of friendly uncle.
sentences.zh: 这使得大流士——我认为他显然不是一个十分讨人喜欢的人——能够把自己塑造成一个慈祥的叔叔形象。

sentences.en: So this is one of, one of his proclamations.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他的宣言之一。

sentences.en: I am the kind of man who is a friend to the right, who frowns upon the wrong, who has no wish to see the weak oppressed by the strong.
sentences.zh: 我是那种与正义为友、对邪恶蹙眉、不愿看到弱者被强者压迫的人。

sentences.en: And so he's basically saying that if you submit to me, you know, it's not a humiliation, it's not a conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是在说，如果你向我臣服，你知道的，这不是一种屈辱，也不是一种征服。

sentences.en: You are blessed.
sentences.zh: 你是受到祝福的。

sentences.en: You've been absorbed into the eternal order of the cosmos.
sentences.zh: 你已经被融入了宇宙的永恒秩序之中。

sentences.en: And what this means in turn, of course, is that if the empire of the Persians is to be cast as a kind of earthly reflection of the divine order of the cosmos,
sentences.zh: 当然，反过来说，这意味着如果波斯帝国要被塑造为宇宙神圣秩序在世俗的反映，

sentences.en: then it means that all those peoples who are not in the empire, who lurk on the fringes of it, that they belong to the dimensions of the lie,
sentences.zh: 那么这就意味着所有那些不在帝国境内、潜伏在帝国边缘的人民，他们都属于虚谎的维度，

sentences.en: that they are essentially worshippers of demons.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上是恶魔的崇拜者。

sentences.en: So is the implication that the Persian Empire, you know, is it absolutely explicit that the Persian Empire will effectively become universal?
sentences.zh: 所以这是否暗示着波斯帝国，你知道的，是否绝对明确地表明波斯帝国将实际上变得无所不包？

sentences.en: Because if this is about divine order, surely there can be nowhere on earth that is beyond the reach of the divine order, right?
sentences.zh: 因为如果这关乎神圣秩序，地球上肯定没有哪个地方能超出神圣秩序的触及范围，对吧？

sentences.en: That's why he's the king of kings.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他是万王之王。

sentences.en: It's why he's the king of lands.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他是万国之王。

sentences.en: It's kind of implicit in those titles.
sentences.zh: 这在这些头衔中是不言而喻的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is a kind of universalizing dream.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种普世化的梦想。

sentences.en: And that means that Darius feels he has the perfect right to go around attacking people beyond the frontiers of the empire.
sentences.zh: 这意味着大流士觉得他有绝对的权利四处攻击帝国边境以外的人。

sentences.en: And high on the list of people that he wants to attack are people that the Greeks call the Scythians and that the Persians call the Saka.
sentences.zh: 在他想要攻击的人员名单上，名列前茅的是希腊人称之为西徐亚人、波斯人称之为萨卡人的人。

sentences.en: And these are horsemen who lurk in the steppes to the north of the Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 这些是潜伏在波斯帝国以北草原上的骑马民族。

sentences.en: They have tall, pointy hats.
sentences.zh: 他们戴着高高的尖顶帽。

sentences.en: They love a bong.
sentences.zh: 他们酷爱大麻烟枪。

sentences.en: They're incredibly proficient horsemen.
sentences.zh: 他们是极其精湛的骑手。

sentences.en: And Darius decides it's time to pacify them, to bring truth and order to the steppelands.
sentences.zh: 大流士决定是时候安抚他们，把真理与秩序带到草原地区了。

sentences.en: And so he decides that he's going to attack them in the weSt.
sentences.zh: 因此他决定从西方进攻他们。

sentences.en: So he arrives in Sardis with an enormous expedition.
sentences.zh: 于是他带着庞大的远征军抵达萨迪斯。

sentences.en: And Sardis, of course, we said, is the capital of the Lydian kings.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们说过，萨迪斯是吕底亚国王的首都。

sentences.en: And it's now the seat of the satrap, the provincial governor of Anatolia.
sentences.zh: 它现在是安纳托利亚总督（即行省长官）的驻地。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Artafernes, who is Darius's brother.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫阿塔弗尼斯，是大流士的兄弟。

sentences.en: And Artafernes means literally the splendor of Arta, the splendor of truth and order.
sentences.zh: 阿塔弗尼斯字面上的意思就是阿塔的光辉，真理与秩序的光辉。

sentences.en: So it's a very kind of appropriate name.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常贴切的名字。

sentences.en: And Artafernes is the governor, not just of Lydia, but of the Ionian Greeks as well on the Aegean coaSt.
sentences.zh: 阿塔弗尼斯不仅是吕底亚的总督，也是爱琴海沿岸爱奥尼亚希腊人的总督。

sentences.en: So Darius is now kind of emerging for the first time into the kind of the Greek area.
sentences.zh: 所以大流士现在某种程度上首次进入了希腊地区。

sentences.en: Sorry, I'm just trying to understand his sense of geography.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我只是在试图理解他的地理概念。

sentences.en: He wants to attack the Scythians, which are who are basically in where are they?
sentences.zh: 他想进攻西徐亚人，而他们基本上在——他们在哪里？

sentences.en: Are they in Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 他们在乌克兰吗？

sentences.en: All the kind of the steppelands north of Persia.
sentences.zh: 所有波斯以北的草原地区。

sentences.en: So Darius, by this point, has already attacked them beyond the Caucasus.
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，大流士已经在高加索山脉以北袭击过他们了。

sentences.en: He's launched an invasion there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里发动了一场入侵。

sentences.en: He's kind of pacified them.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上安抚了他们。

sentences.en: And now he wants to attack the tribes who lurk kind of beyond the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 现在他想进攻潜伏在黑海以外的部落。

sentences.en: So he's going a very elaborate roundabout route, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他走了一条非常复杂且绕远的路线，对吧？

sentences.en: He's going to go up through the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 他要穿过巴尔干半岛。

sentences.en: Yes, I think he wants to expand into Europe.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想他想向欧洲扩张。

sentences.en: I think he wants to kind of to have a foothold there.
sentences.zh: 我想他想在那里建立一个立足点。

sentences.en: I think there are all kinds of various strategic considerations.
sentences.zh: 我想这里有各种各样的战略考量。

sentences.en: But I think he also he hasn't he hasn't really done his homework, because if he had studied the careers of Napoleon or Hitler,
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得他——他根本没做功课，因为如果他研究过拿破仑或希特勒的生平，

sentences.en: he would realize that launching attacks into the the steppelands of Ukraine and and Russia beyond it is not is not a sensible thing to do.
sentences.zh: 他就会意识到向乌克兰草原以及更远处的俄罗斯草原发动进攻并不是明智之举。

sentences.en: Do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: He didn't he hadn't done.
sentences.zh: 他没有——他根本没做。

sentences.en: He hadn't listened to our excellent series about Charles XII and the Great Northern War.
sentences.zh: 他没有听我们关于查理十二世和大北方战争的精彩系列节目。

sentences.en: No, he hadn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: So anyway, he so he's he's inside as he marches north up towards the Hellespont, which is the straits between Asia and Europe, crosses them, goes up to the Danube,
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，他在萨迪斯内部向北进军，走向赫勒斯滂（即亚洲和欧洲之间的海峡），渡过海峡，一直走到多瑙河，

sentences.en: builds a pontoon bridge across the Danube and vanishes into the steppelands.
sentences.zh: 在多瑙河上建造了一座浮桥，然后消失在草原深处。

sentences.en: And unsurprisingly, the campaign proves a disaster because the Scythians on their horses adopt a scorched earth policy,
sentences.zh: 毫不意外，这场战役以灾难告终，因为骑着马的西徐亚人采取了焦土政策，

sentences.en: as the Russians and the Ukrainians and so on will do many times in the future.
sentences.zh: 就像俄罗斯人和乌克兰人等在未来多次做的那样。

sentences.en: And Darius finds it impossible to corner them.
sentences.zh: 大流士发现根本无法将他们逼入绝境。

sentences.en: He's basically the first imperial invader to discover that it's not actually very easy to conquer the steppelands.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是第一个发现征服草原其实并不那么容易的帝国入侵者。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, in his rear by this pontoon bridge on the Danube,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在多瑙河浮桥的后方，

sentences.en: there is also danger lurking because Darius has set kind of squadrons to guard the pontoon bridge to make sure that no one attacks it.
sentences.zh: 也潜藏着危险，因为大流士派出了分队去守卫浮桥，以确保没有人袭击它。

sentences.en: And one of the people who've been set to guard this pontoon bridge is actively treacherous, is actively plotting the ruin and destruction of Darius.
sentences.zh: 而被派去守卫这座浮桥的人中，有一个人居心叵测，正在积极策划大流士的灭亡与毁灭。

sentences.en: So these guards are the Greeks, the Greeks who are subject to Darius.
sentences.zh: 所以这些守卫是希腊人，臣服于大流士的希腊人。

sentences.en: They are the rulers of the various Ionian cities that dot the Aegean seaboard of what is now Turkey.
sentences.zh: 他们是星罗棋布于现今土耳其爱琴海沿岸的各个爱奥尼亚城市的统治者。

sentences.en: And these rulers are what the Greeks call tyrannoi, from which we get the English word tyrant.
sentences.zh: 这些统治者就是希腊人所说的“僭主”（tyrannoi），英语单词“暴君”（tyrant）便源于此。

sentences.en: But I think tyrant doesn't convey the right sense.
sentences.zh: 但我认为“暴君”并不能传达出准确的含义。

sentences.en: Essentially, populist strongmen, they are Peron rather than Hitler.
sentences.zh: 本质上是民粹主义强人，比起希特勒，他们更像是庇隆。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of a better analogy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个更好的类比。

sentences.en: And they are pretty loyal to the Persians because the Persians keep them in power.
sentences.zh: 他们对波斯人相当忠诚，因为波斯人让他们维持权柄。

sentences.en: However, the Persians use them as their tools to subdue kind of popular risings or whatever in these various Greek cities.
sentences.zh: 然而，波斯人利用他们作为工具来平息这些希腊城市的民众起义之类的事情。

sentences.en: However, there is one tyrannos there.
sentences.zh: 不过，那里有一个僭主，

sentences.en: So kind of populist strongman who is not Ionian.
sentences.zh: 也就是说一个并非爱奥尼亚人的民粹主义强人。

sentences.en: And he's the ruler of a very recently founded colony.
sentences.zh: 他是某个近期才建立的殖民地的统治者。

sentences.en: And he's an aristocrat from a city on the far western side of the Aegean in mainland Greece.
sentences.zh: 他是来自希腊本土爱琴海最西侧一座城市的贵族。

sentences.en: And this city is Athens.
sentences.zh: 这座城市就是雅典。

sentences.en: And the name of this tyrannos is Miltiades.
sentences.zh: 这个僭主的名字叫米太得。

sentences.en: And he is very able.
sentences.zh: 他非常能干。

sentences.en: He's very ruthless.
sentences.zh: 他非常冷酷无情。

sentences.en: And he's ambitious, I would say, to the point of overreach.
sentences.zh: 而且依我看，他的野心大到有些过头了。

sentences.en: And he had sailed from Athens to what the ancients called the Thracian Chersonese, which is the thin peninsula which forms the European side of the Hellespont.
sentences.zh: 他曾从雅典航行到古代人所说的色雷斯切索尼萨，也就是构成赫勒斯滂欧洲一侧的狭长半岛。

sentences.en: And today is called Gallipoli.
sentences.zh: 如今它被称为加里波利。

sentences.en: Yeah, we'll be hearing a bit more about Gallipoli in a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 对，几周后我们会听到更多关于加里波利的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, in a few weeks' time.
sentences.zh: 对，几周之后。

sentences.en: So Miltiades, he set up this colony on the Thracian Chersonese, a.k.a.
sentences.zh: 所以米太得在色雷斯切索尼萨建立了这个殖民地，也就是加里波利。

sentences.en: Gallipoli.
sentences.zh: 加里波利。

sentences.en: And he's done it partly because the Hellespont is really, really important to Athens.
sentences.zh: 他这么做部分是因为赫勒斯滂对雅典来说真的、真的很重要。

sentences.en: Athens is dependent for its food supply on grain from the Chersonese and also from the Crimea, so the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 雅典的粮食供应依赖于来自切索尼萨以及克里米亚（即黑海）的谷物。

sentences.en: But I think he's also done it because he's a bit of a lone wolf.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他这么做也是因为他有点独来独往。

sentences.en: He enjoys the exercise of power.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢行使权力。

sentences.en: And this is why he rules the Chersonese, not as a Democrat or anything like that, but as an out-and-out strong man.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他统治切索尼萨不是作为一个民主主义者或诸如此类的人，而是作为一个地地道道的强人。

sentences.en: He has a 500-strong bodyguard.
sentences.zh: 他拥有五百人的保镖队伍。

sentences.en: He's married into the local aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 他与当地贵族联姻。

sentences.en: He's been busy throwing his weight around.
sentences.zh: 他一直在耀武扬威。

sentences.en: And that's why he's infuriated that Darius has turned up, made him submit, and kind of ruined his fun to an extent.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么大流士的出现、迫使他屈服并在某种程度上毁了他的乐子让他愤怒不已。

sentences.en: And so he comes up with this cunning plan.
sentences.zh: 于是他想出了一个狡猾的计划。

sentences.en: Why don't we just cut the pontoon bridge and leave the Persians stranded on the northern bank?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不直接砍断浮桥，把波斯人困在北岸呢？

sentences.en: Like, you know, it's a kind of brilliant idea.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，这真是一个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: But high risk, right?
sentences.zh: 但风险极高，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the retribution of the Persians would be swift and merciless.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，波斯人的报复将是迅速而毫不留情的。

sentences.en: And the other strong men, the Ionian strong men, they're not going to go for this, are they?
sentences.zh: 而其他的强人，那些爱奥尼亚强人，是不会同意这一点的，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, no, because, to quote Herodotus, there was not one of them, but he owed his position as Tyrannos to Darius.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，因为，用希罗多德的话来说，他们当中没有一个人不是将自己作为僭主的地位归功于大流士的。

sentences.en: So, in other words, they are, you know, they're the kind of the Vichy-type rulers of the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们，你知道的，他们有点像希腊人当中的维希政权式统治者。

sentences.en: You don't want to go attacking your sponsor.
sentences.zh: 你可不想去攻击你的金主。

sentences.en: And there's one guy in particular, one Ionian Tyrannos, who particularly presses this.
sentences.zh: 有一个人格外坚持这一点，他是一个爱奥尼亚僭主。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Histaeus.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫希斯泰伊乌斯。

sentences.en: And Histaeus is the ruler of the most powerful of all the various Ionian cities.
sentences.zh: 希斯泰伊乌斯是所有爱奥尼亚城市中最强大的那座城市的统治者。

sentences.en: It's the largeSt.
sentences.zh: 它是最大的。

sentences.en: It's the richeSt.
sentences.zh: 它是最富有的。

sentences.en: It's the most sophisticated of the Ionian cities.
sentences.zh: 它是爱奥尼亚诸城中最精致的。

sentences.en: And this is a place called Miletus.
sentences.zh: 这个地方叫米利都。

sentences.en: And it has four great harbors full of shipping from across the Mediterranean, from across the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 它拥有四个巨大的港口，停满了来自地中海各地、黑海各地的商船。

sentences.en: It's the birthplace of philosophy.
sentences.zh: 它是哲学的发源地。

sentences.en: It's the birthplace of history.
sentences.zh: 它是历史的发源地。

sentences.en: It's the birthplace of what ultimately one might call science.
sentences.zh: 它是最终可被称为科学的发源地。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an absolute intellectual powerhouse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个绝对的知识重镇。

sentences.en: And it is praised as the glory of Ionia.
sentences.zh: 它被赞誉为爱奥尼亚的荣耀。

sentences.en: And Histaeus does not want to risk the prosperity and glory and wealth of his city.
sentences.zh: 而希斯泰伊乌斯不想拿他城市的繁荣、荣耀和财富去冒风险。

sentences.en: And so he essentially crushes Miltiades' proposal.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上粉碎了米太得的提议。

sentences.en: Darius returns from his abortive attack on the Scythians.
sentences.zh: 大流士从对西徐亚人的无果进攻中归来。

sentences.en: He crosses the pontoon.
sentences.zh: 他穿过了浮桥。

sentences.en: And Histaeus is rewarded for his loyalty with splendid gifts, grants of land, the favor of the king of kings.
sentences.zh: 作为对他忠诚的回报，希斯提亚伊乌斯获得了丰厚的礼物、土地赏赐以及万王之王的青睐。

sentences.en: And among the grants of land that Histaeus gets is a region of Thrace that Darius had just recently conquered.
sentences.zh: 在希斯提亚伊乌斯获得的土地赏赐中，有一处是色雷斯的一个地区，那是大流士最近刚刚征服的地方。

sentences.en: And this is a place called Myrcanus.
sentences.zh: 这个地方叫做米尔卡努斯。

sentences.en: And Myrcanus has silver mines and it has forests.
sentences.zh: 米尔卡努斯有银矿，也有森林。

sentences.en: And forests are obviously useful for building a fleet.
sentences.zh: 森林显然对建造舰队很有用。

sentences.en: And I think the ambition of Histaeus is to exploit the favor of Darius and the backing of the Persian governor that Histaeus can enjoy to build a kind of semi-independent power base for himself in the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 我认为希斯提亚伊乌斯的野心是利用大流士的青睐以及他所能享有的波斯总督的支持，在爱琴海为自己建立某种半独立的权力基地。

sentences.en: You know, he will remain loyal to the Persians in Myletus.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他将在米利都保持对波斯的忠诚。

sentences.en: But if he can establish, you know, a kind of sub-empire in the Aegean, in Thrace, say the northern coastline of the Aegean, you know, that'd be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 但如果他能在爱琴海，在色雷斯，比如说爱琴海的北部海岸线，建立起某种类似微型帝国的势力，你知道的，那可就太棒了。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: That'd be great.
sentences.zh: 那将好极了。

sentences.en: But that doesn't work out, right?
sentences.zh: 但这并没有成功，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he ends up with an unexpected promotion.
sentences.zh: 因为他最终得到了一次意料之外的晋升。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think possibly because the Persians are a little bit twitchy about this, you know, it's a good way to stop his regional ambitions,
sentences.zh: 我想可能是因为波斯人对此感到有些不安，你知道的，这是阻止他地区野心的一個好方法，

sentences.en: which is essentially is to kick him upstairs.
sentences.zh: 也就是实质上把他明升暗降。

sentences.en: So he gets promoted to the rank of royal table companion.
sentences.zh: 于是他被晋升为王室座上宾。

sentences.en: So that means he has to leave Myletus and head to Persia and kind of hang out in Persepolis and Susa, the other great palace complex that Darius has.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他不得不离开米利都，前往波斯，在波斯波利斯和苏萨——大流士拥有的另一处宏伟宫殿群——消磨时光。

sentences.en: And it's essentially a kind of gilded cage because he enjoys tremendous, you know, wealth and all of that, the favor of the king.
sentences.zh: 这本质上算是一个镀金的笼子，因为他享有巨大的财富以及诸如此类的一切，还有国王的青睐。

sentences.en: But he's a long way from home.
sentences.zh: 但他离家太远了。

sentences.en: He can't kind of build this empire that he'd been hoping to do.
sentences.zh: 他无法建立他一直期盼的这个帝国。

sentences.en: However, all is not lost for his deus because his family retains its rule of Myletus.
sentences.zh: 不过，对于希斯提亚伊乌斯来说，并非一切都失去了，因为他的家族保留了对米利都的统治。

sentences.en: So his replacement as Tyrannus is his nephew and son-in-law, a guy called Aristagoras.
sentences.zh: 因此，他作为僭主的继任者是他的外甥兼女婿，一个叫阿里斯塔戈拉的人。

sentences.en: And Aristagoras is very ambitious, very wily, very proactive.
sentences.zh: 而阿里斯塔戈拉野心勃勃、非常狡猾且极具主观能动性。

sentences.en: So a chip off the old block.
sentences.zh: 真是有其叔必有其侄。

sentences.en: And Aristagoras has essentially bought into this dream of a kind of family empire in the Aegean that he's inherited from his uncle.
sentences.zh: 阿里斯塔戈拉基本上已经全盘接受了从他叔叔那里继承来的、在爱琴海建立家族帝国的梦想。

sentences.en: He's very keen to do that.
sentences.zh: 他非常热衷于这样做。

sentences.en: He is also aware that there are all kinds of social tensions in Myletus itself, that there are conspiracies, that there are whisperings,
sentences.zh: 他也意识到米利都本身存在着各种社会矛盾，有阴谋，有流言，

sentences.en: that there are plots to topple the tyranny and introduce a democracy.
sentences.zh: 有推翻暴政并引入民主制的密谋。

sentences.en: So these social tensions, you know, he feels like he's essentially sitting on the edge of a volcano.
sentences.zh: 所以这些社会矛盾，你知道的，让他觉得自己简直就像坐在火山边缘。

sentences.en: And that's another incentive to try and go out into the Aegean and kind of carve out a small empire for himself, because that would then generate more wealth,
sentences.zh: 这是促使他尝试去爱琴海开拓一个小帝国的另一个动力，因为那将带来更多的财富，

sentences.en: which would enable him to kind of keep the lid on this pressure cooker.
sentences.zh: 这将使他能够勉强压住这个压力锅。

sentences.en: And so he cooks up what seems to him a brilliant plan.
sentences.zh: 于是他琢磨出了一个在他看来绝妙的计划。

sentences.en: And this plan is designed to boost his dynasty's power, to consolidate his relations with the Persians, and thereby to keep agitation for a democracy in Myletus firmly in check.
sentences.zh: 这个计划旨在增强他王朝的权势，巩固他与波斯人的关系，从而将米利都对民主制的呼声死死压制住。

sentences.en: And the plan is, he will lead an expedition against the island of Naxos, which lies in the middle of the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 这个计划是：他将领导一场针对纳克索斯岛的远征，该岛位于爱琴海中部。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of stepping stone between what's now the Turkish coastline of the Aegean and mainland Greece.
sentences.zh: 所以它算是连接现在的爱琴海土耳其海岸线和希腊本土的一个跳板。

sentences.en: And you could see the appeal of that to the Persians if they ever want to launch an attack on mainland Greece.
sentences.zh: 如果波斯人想对希腊本土发动进攻，你可以看出这对他们有多大吸引力。

sentences.en: Naxos would be very useful to them.
sentences.zh: 纳克索斯对他们将非常有用。

sentences.en: And so Aristagoras goes to Artafernes.
sentences.zh: 于是阿里斯塔戈拉去找阿尔塔费尔内斯。

sentences.en: So Artafernes, to remind people, is the Persian governor of Sardis.
sentences.zh: 提醒大家一下，阿尔塔费尔内斯是萨尔迪斯的波斯总督。

sentences.en: He is Darius' brother, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是大流士的兄弟，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And his name means the splendor of Arta.
sentences.zh: 他的名字意思是阿尔塔的光辉。

sentences.en: So anyone getting muddled up between Aristagoras and Artafernes, if it's got Arta in it, it's a Persian.
sentences.zh: 所以任何人如果把阿里斯塔戈拉和阿尔塔费尔内斯搞混了，只要名字里带阿尔塔的，就是波斯人。

sentences.en: Okay, perfect.
sentences.zh: 好吧，太完美了。

sentences.en: So Artafernes, the governor, says, yeah, all right.
sentences.zh: 于是总督阿尔塔费尔内斯说，行，好吧。

sentences.en: Okay, fair enough.
sentences.zh: 好吧，倒也合情合理。

sentences.en: I'll need to check it with my brother.
sentences.zh: 我需要跟我兄弟确认一下。

sentences.en: So he checks with Darius and Darius says, yeah, okay, why not?
sentences.zh: 于是他向大流士确认，大流士说，行，好吧，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And so Aristagoras is able to go to launch an expedition with the deployment of 200 ships that have been given to him by the Persians for the expedition.
sentences.zh: 因此，阿里斯塔戈拉得以发起远征，动用了波斯人为此次远征提供给他的200艘战舰。

sentences.en: And he's accompanied by a Persian admiral called Megabates, basically to kind of keep an eye on Aristagoras.
sentences.zh: 随行的还有一位名叫梅加巴泰斯的波斯海军上将，基本上是为了监视阿里斯塔戈拉。

sentences.en: And he's Artafernes' cousin.
sentences.zh: 他是阿尔塔费尔内斯的堂弟。

sentences.en: So it's, again, all very much being kept in the family.
sentences.zh: 所以说，这又是一场彻头彻尾的家族内部运作。

sentences.en: And so Megabates and Aristagoras set sail with these 200 ships for Naxos in 499.
sentences.zh: 于是梅加巴泰斯和阿里斯塔戈拉在公元前499年率领这200艘战舰起航前往纳克索斯。

sentences.en: But it's an absolute disaster.
sentences.zh: 但这是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: The main city of Naxos is put under siege and it just drags by one month, two months, three months, four months.
sentences.zh: 纳克索斯的主城遭到围困，结果一拖就是一个月、两个月、三个月、四个月。

sentences.en: And after four months, Aristagoras has used up all his money.
sentences.zh: 四个月后，阿里斯塔戈拉花光了所有的钱。

sentences.en: The Naxians are still holding out.
sentences.zh: 纳克索斯人仍然在坚守。

sentences.en: And Megabates says, look, come on, this is hopeless.
sentences.zh: 梅加巴泰斯说，听着，得了吧，这没指望了。

sentences.en: We're giving up.
sentences.zh: 我们放弃吧。

sentences.en: There's no way we're carrying on with this.
sentences.zh: 我们绝无可能继续下去了。

sentences.en: You've essentially, you know, you told us this would be easy.
sentences.zh: 你基本上，你知道的，你告诉我们这很简单。

sentences.en: It isn't.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: You know, you're in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你惹上大麻烦了。

sentences.en: We're heading back.
