sentences.en: And of course, there's no way the Athenians are going to do this.
sentences.zh: 他们已经有了民主制。

sentences.en: They've got their democracy.
sentences.zh: 他们已经把暴君赶跑了。

sentences.en: They've thrown the tyrant out.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让他回来。

sentences.en: They don't want him back.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拒绝了。

sentences.en: And so they say no.
sentences.zh: 阿尔塔费尔内斯对此没有任何回应。

sentences.en: And there's no response to this from Artafernes.
sentences.zh: 但有一种挥之不去的焦虑，那就是，也许波斯人会为此来惩罚我们。

sentences.en: But there is a kind of nagging anxiety that, well, perhaps the Persians will come and punish us for this.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，阿里斯塔戈拉斯带着他的建议到来，邀请雅典人加入伊奥尼亚起义，似乎为雅典人提供了一个掌握主动权的机会。

sentences.en: And so I think that the arrival of Aristagoras with his suggestion that the Athenians join the Ionian revolt, it seems to offer the Athenians a chance to get onto the front foot.
sentences.zh: 必须强调的是，雅典人对波斯人其实一无所知。

sentences.en: And it has to be emphasized that the Athenians don't really know anything about the Persians.
sentences.zh: 而且，阿里斯塔戈拉斯还对他们说，哦，波斯人绝对是懦夫。

sentences.en: And also, Aristagoras is telling them, oh, the Persians are absolute wusses.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们就是一群娘们儿。

sentences.en: You know, they're a bunch of women.
sentences.zh: 他们还穿裤子。

sentences.en: They wear trousers.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 波斯分明是世界上压倒性最强的超级大国，雅典人怎么会对其一无所知呢？

sentences.en: How can the Athenians not know about the Persians when Persia is by far the world's most preponderant power?
sentences.zh: 希腊人相当孤陋寡闻。

sentences.en: Greeks are pretty insular.
sentences.zh: 他们相当孤陋寡闻。

sentences.en: They're pretty insular.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想他们多少有点模糊的意识。

sentences.en: I mean, they're kind of vaguely aware of it, I think.
sentences.zh: 但他们又不能在互联网上阅读关于波斯的内容。

sentences.en: But it's not like they can read about the Persians on the internet.
sentences.zh: 据推测，他们会与伊奥尼亚城市保持联系，而这些城市是波斯势力范围的一部分。

sentences.en: They would have contacts with the Ionian cities, presumably, which are part of the Persian orbit.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们会的。

sentences.en: Yeah, they would.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们可能把波斯人等同于吕底亚人过去的模样。

sentences.en: But I think that they probably equate the Persians to the way that the Lydians had been.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们是一种区域性霸主。

sentences.en: You know, they're a kind of regional overlord.
sentences.zh: 他们可能根本没有意识到波斯帝国有多么辽阔，波斯国王可调配的资源有多么巨大。

sentences.en: They probably don't have a sense of just how vast the Persian empire is and how immense the resources available to the Persian king.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不管出于什么原因，他们决定，好吧，行，我们加入你们。

sentences.en: I mean, whatever the reason is, they decide, yeah, OK, we'll join you.
sentences.zh: 于是在公元前498年春天，由民主制国家派遣去进攻伊朗（编者注：应为波斯）军队的有史以来第一支特遣部队扬帆横渡爱琴海，这是一支由20艘船组成的舰队。

sentences.en: And so in the spring of 498, the first ever task force sent by a democracy to attack an Iranian army, set sail across the Aegean, and it's a fleet of 20 ships.
sentences.zh: 它并不是独自航行的，因为还有另一个希腊城市落入了阿里斯塔戈拉斯的甜言蜜语之中。

sentences.en: And it doesn't sail alone because there is another Greek city that falls for the blandishments of Aristagoras.
sentences.zh: 这个地方叫埃雷特里亚，是附近埃维亚岛上的一个商业城市。

sentences.en: And this is a place called Eretria, which is a merchant city on the nearby island of Euboea.
sentences.zh: 所以埃维亚，如果你想想希腊的地图，阿提卡向爱琴海突出一块，在阿提卡北部海岸的正上方有一个狭长的岛屿。

sentences.en: So Euboea, if you think of the map of Greece, Attica sticking out into the Aegean, there's a long, narrow island directly above the northern coast of Attica.
sentences.zh: 那就是埃维亚，今天人们称之为埃维亚岛。

sentences.en: And that's Euboea, Evia, as it's called today.
sentences.zh: 用希罗多德的话说，可怕的灾难将从这些船只中降临，无论是对希腊人还是对蛮族而言——希罗多德这里指的就是波斯人。

sentences.en: And in the words of Herodotus, terrible evils would stem from these ships, both for the Greeks and the barbarians, by which Herodotus means the Persians.
sentences.zh: 但起初，对希腊人来说一切都很顺利，不是吗？

sentences.en: But at first, it all goes well for the Greeks, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们与伊奥尼亚人会合了，雅典人和埃雷特里亚人。

sentences.en: I mean, they join up with the Ionians, the Athenians and the Eritreans.
sentences.zh: 他们向萨尔迪斯进军。

sentences.en: They march to Sardis.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔塔费尔内斯——提醒大家一下，他就是总督。

sentences.en: So Artafernes, who is, to remind people, he is the governor.
sentences.zh: 他是大流士的兄弟。

sentences.en: He is Teraeus' brother.
sentences.zh: 他最终基本上被围困在自己卫城的堡垒中了。

sentences.en: He ends up being basically barricaded in his own acropolis in the sort of citadel.
sentences.zh: 他们洗劫并焚烧了萨尔迪斯的下城。

sentences.en: And they loot and burn the lower city of Sardis.
sentences.zh: 但随后，你认为现实开始向他们袭来吗？

sentences.en: But then, do you think reality starts to dawn on them?
sentences.zh: 波斯人可能比他们预想的更可怕？

sentences.en: The Persians might be more formidable than they had anticipated?
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I think it does.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们非常迅速地开始意识到自己接了个啃不动的大骨头。

sentences.en: I think they very rapidly start to realize that they've bitten off much more than they could chew.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为焚烧库柏勒神庙让他们非常不安，因为他们现在担心自己会招致大地女神的愤怒。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the burning of the Temple of Kiblae is very unsettling for them, because they are now anxious that they will draw down the wrath of the mother goddess.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，听着，我们得回去了。

sentences.en: And so they say, well, look, we're getting back.
sentences.zh: 这事一点也不顺利。

sentences.en: This isn't going well at all.
sentences.zh: 他们从萨尔迪斯撤回海岸。

sentences.en: And they head back from Sardis to the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 正当他们接近海岸时，雅典人和伊奥尼亚人遭到了一次袭击，

sentences.en: And as they're drawing near to the coast, the Athenians and the Ionians get attacked by
sentences.zh: 来者是波斯骑兵，雅典人以前从未与这种部队交过手。

sentences.en: Persian cavalry, which the Athenians have never come up against before.
sentences.zh: 他们溃不成军。

sentences.en: And they're routed.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是雅典人真正意识到的时候：其实，这些根本不是一群娘们儿，尽管他们可能穿着裤子。

sentences.en: And I think this is the moment when the Athenians realize, actually, you know, this isn't, these aren't a bunch of women, even though they may wear trousers.
sentences.zh: 这些是可怕的战士。

sentences.en: These are terrifying fighters.
sentences.zh: 尤其是骑兵。

sentences.en: And the cavalry in particular.
sentences.zh: 希腊并不是一个适合使用骑兵的土地，而伊朗（编者注：此处指波斯高原）平坦的高原则绝对鼓励骑兵的使用。

sentences.en: Greece is not a land that encourages the use of cavalry, whereas the flat plateau of Iran absolutely encourages the use of cavalry.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，构成希腊军队的主力步兵——重装步兵，被称为拥有重装装备（hoplite）的人。

sentences.en: And essentially, the kind of the heavy infantry that forms a Greek army, hoplites, they're called people with the hopler, the kind of heavy kit.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在开阔地上被波斯骑兵缠上，他们就完蛋了。

sentences.en: If they get caught in open land by Persian cavalry, they are toaSt.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是现在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And this is pretty much what happens now.
sentences.zh: 雅典军队遭到了极其残酷的蹂躏。

sentences.en: The Athenian force is very brutally savaged.
sentences.zh: 幸存者逃回船上，并表示我们要离开这里。

sentences.en: Those who survive get back to their ships and they say, we are out of here.
sentences.zh: 我们可不在这儿死扛。

sentences.en: We're not sticking around.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们基本上一直在对我们撒谎。

sentences.en: You know, you've you've you've basically lied to us.
sentences.zh: 他们把这番话告诉了阿里斯塔戈拉斯，而阿里斯塔戈拉斯苦苦哀求他们不要走。

sentences.en: They tell Aristagoras and Aristagoras is kind of begging them not to go.
sentences.zh: 但雅典人说，不，我们要撤了。

sentences.en: But the Athenians say, no, we're off.
sentences.zh: 他们扬帆横渡爱琴海返回，并对所有后续的求援置之不理。

sentences.en: And they sail back across the Aegean and they ignore all future appeals.
sentences.zh: 我想他们的计划基本上就是希望波斯人把这事忘得一干二净，并且假装这一切从未发生过。

sentences.en: And I think that their plan is basically to hope that the Persians will forget all about it and they will pretend that it never happened.
sentences.zh: 这就好比《宋飞正传》里的那个场景：乔治宣布他要离开，然后意识到自己犯了一个可怕的错误，于是又走回去，试图假装

sentences.en: It's like that scene in Seinfeld where George announces that he's he's leaving and then realize he's made a terrible mistake and just goes back in and tries to pretend that
sentences.zh: 这事从未发生过。

sentences.en: it had never happened.
sentences.zh: 我认为这基本上就是他们的策略——假装这一切从未发生过。

sentences.en: I think that is basically the strategy to pretend that it had never happened.
sentences.zh: 起初，这看起来是个合理的策略，因为事实上波斯的重心非常集中在粉碎伊奥尼亚人身上。

sentences.en: And to begin with, it looks a reasonable strategy because actually the Persian focus is on very much on crushing the Ionians.
sentences.zh: 他们才是公开的叛军。

sentences.en: They are the ones who are the open rebels.
sentences.zh: 这花了他们四年时间。

sentences.en: And it takes them four years.
sentences.zh: 当然，当胜利最终到来时，正如预料的那样是毫不留情的。

sentences.en: And of course, when victory finally comes, it is predictably merciless.
sentences.zh: 于是在公元前494年，伊奥尼亚舰队在米利都郊外的一个名叫拉尔德的岛屿附近被摧毁。

sentences.en: So in 494, the Ionian fleet is destroyed off an island called Larde, which is an island just outside Miletus.
sentences.zh: 米利都遭到突袭攻陷。

sentences.en: Miletus is stormed.
sentences.zh: 这里的男人被屠杀。

sentences.en: Her men are slaughtered.
sentences.zh: 这里的女人被强暴。

sentences.en: Her women raped.
sentences.zh: 这里的男孩被阉割。

sentences.en: Her son's castrated.
sentences.zh: 这里的女孩被沦为奴隶。

sentences.en: Her daughter's enslaved.
sentences.zh: 随后，幸存者被从爱琴海海岸驱赶出去，一路驱逐到波斯帝国的腹地——伊朗，

sentences.en: And the survivors are then sent off from the coast of the Aegean all the way into the depths of the
sentences.zh: 送往劳改营、后宫，或者不管什么地方，总之是奴隶市场。

sentences.en: Persian Empire to Iran, to work camps, to harems, to whatever, to the slave markets.
sentences.zh: 当他们被押送着——用锁链串成一串向前走时，他们与迎面而来的定居者擦肩而过，这些定居者是被阿尔塔费尔内斯赐予了土地的人。

sentences.en: And as they are being led off, you know, chained in coffles, they pass settlers coming the other way who have been granted their lands by Artafernes.
sentences.zh: 而那些没有被流放的少数米利都人，则只能在伊奥尼亚昔日辉煌、这处伟大哲学发源地那被烧焦的

sentences.en: And those few Milesians who have not been deported are left to, you know, huddle up amid the blackened
sentences.zh: 废墟中瑟瑟发抖。

sentences.en: ruins of what had been the glory of Ionia, this great birthplace of philosophy.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个毁灭性的时刻，不仅对伊奥尼亚人，对雅典人也是如此。

sentences.en: So it is a devastating moment, and not just for the Ionians, but for the Athenians as well.
sentences.zh: 于是上演了一出描绘米利都毁灭的悲剧，观众们异常沮丧，以至于写下它的剧作家被罚款了。

sentences.en: So a tragedy is staged illustrating the destruction of Miletus, and the audience are so upset that the playwright who wrote it is fined.
sentences.zh: 大家一致认为，还是那句话，咱们就别再谈这事了。

sentences.en: And it's agreed that, you know, again, let's just not talk about this.
sentences.zh: 然而，即使在米利都毁灭之后，战场上仍然有两名伊奥尼亚叛军领袖。

sentences.en: However, even after the destruction of Miletus, there are two Ionian rebel leaders still in the field.
sentences.zh: 这里面不包括阿里斯塔戈拉斯。

sentences.en: These did not include Aristagoras.
sentences.zh: 此时他已经死了。

sentences.en: By this point, he is dead.
sentences.zh: 他在公元前497年就已经在一场卑劣的斗殴中丧生了，地点就在米尔卡努斯，他

sentences.en: He had been killed back in 497 in a kind of a squalid brawl in his, in Myrcanus, his private
sentences.zh: 在色雷斯的私人领地上。

sentences.en: Thracian fiefdom.
sentences.zh: 但他的叔叔希斯泰乌斯依然活跃在场上。

sentences.en: But his uncle, Histaeus, is still on the scene.
sentences.zh: 所以希斯泰乌斯曾被带到大流士的宫廷里，成为他的座上宾。

sentences.en: So Histaeus had been, this is the guy who had been taken off to Darius's court to be, you know, his table companion.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是一个非常狡猾、奸诈、不可信的人物，总是玩着两面派的把戏。

sentences.en: And he's a very wily, cunning, untrustworthy figure, really, who's always kind of playing double games.
sentences.zh: 他是个老狐狸。

sentences.en: He's an old fox.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 当起义爆发时，他去找大流士说，听着，我是解决这件事的人选。

sentences.en: And when the, when the revolt broke out, he went to Darius and said, look, I'm the guy to solve this.
sentences.zh: 我了解这些人。

sentences.en: I know these people.
sentences.zh: 把我送回去吧。

sentences.en: Send me back.
sentences.zh: 把我送回去。

sentences.en: And so Darius does.
sentences.zh: 大流士确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And Histaeus turns up in Sardis very coolly.
sentences.zh: 希斯提埃乌斯大摇大摆地回到了萨底斯。

sentences.en: And Artafernes has entirely sussed him out.
sentences.zh: 阿塔费尔内斯早就把他的底细摸得一清二楚了。

sentences.en: And he says to him, Aristagoras may have worn the shoe, but you were the one who made it.
sentences.zh: 他对他说，阿里斯托格拉图斯虽然穿了鞋，但这双鞋是你亲手做的。

sentences.en: In other words, you are the guy who fostered this rebellion.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你就是这场叛乱的幕后推手。

sentences.en: And Herodotus tells a brilliant story about how actually it was Histaeus who had persuaded
sentences.zh: 希罗多德讲了一个精彩的故事，说实际上是希斯提埃乌斯劝说

sentences.en: Aristagoras to launch the rebellion.
sentences.zh: 阿里斯托格拉图斯发动了叛乱。

sentences.en: And Histaeus had done this by getting a slave, shaving his head, tattooing a message on the scalp.
sentences.zh: 希斯提埃乌斯的方法是找一个奴隶，剃光他的头，在头皮上刺字。

sentences.en: You know, basically let's have a revolt, letting the hair back and then sending the slave to
sentences.zh: 你知道的，基本上就是煽动起义，等头发长长后再把奴隶派往

sentences.en: Aristagoras with the, and the slave has to say, shave my head.
sentences.zh: 阿里斯托格拉图斯那里，而且奴隶必须说：‘剃光我的头。’

sentences.en: Um, so whether that's true or not, most historians, I think, uh, probably think that's a tall story, but there are some who, who, who give it credence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以不管这是真是假，我想大多数历史学家大概都认为这是一个离奇的故事，但也有一些人对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: And Histaeus, when he arrives in Iona, he's been playing a kind of very shrewd double game,
sentences.zh: 当希斯提埃乌斯抵达伊奥尼亚时，他一直在玩一种非常精明的双重游戏，

sentences.en: but very perilous because he's fomenting rebellion, um, not just among the Ionians, but among
sentences.zh: 但这非常危险，因为他不仅在伊奥尼亚人中煽动叛乱，还在

sentences.en: Artafernes' own, uh, court because Artafernes really hates him.
sentences.zh: 阿塔费尔内斯自己的宫廷里煽动，因为阿塔费尔内斯真的很恨他。

sentences.en: So Histaeus thinks if I can get rid of Artafernes, that'll be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以希斯提埃乌斯心想，如果我能除掉阿塔费尔内斯，那就太妙了。

sentences.en: It doesn't work out.
sentences.zh: 结果并没有成功。

sentences.en: Um, he gets captured, he gets taken to Sardis, um, Histaeus says, look, send me to Darius,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他被捕了，被带到了萨底斯，希斯提埃乌斯说，听着，把我送到大流士那儿，

sentences.en: I'll be able to explain everything.
sentences.zh: 我能解释一切。

sentences.en: Artafernes says, no way, has him impaled, chops off his head, has it pickled, um, kind of wrapped up in ice, sends it off to Darius.
sentences.zh: 阿塔费尔内斯说，门都没有，直接将他穿刺处决，砍下他的头，用冰块将人头冷冻腌制起来，然后送给大流士。

sentences.en: And Darius, it is said, was sufficiently upset that he gave the head of this rebel a dignified burial.
sentences.zh: 据说大流士为此感到十分难过，于是为这位叛军首领的头颅举行了体面的葬礼。

sentences.en: That's the end of Histaeus.
sentences.zh: 希斯提埃乌斯的故事就此结束。

sentences.en: And we've got one guy left.
sentences.zh: 现在我们只剩下一个家伙了。

sentences.en: So this is Miltiades, who was the Athenian guy who had taken over what's now Gallipoli, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是米提亚德，那个占领了如今加里波利半岛的雅典人，对吧？

sentences.en: So he has fought very bravely and well in the Ionian revolt, but by now the revolt is effectively crushed and the net is closing in on him and a squadron is sent to intercept
sentences.zh: 因此他在伊奥尼亚起义中英勇善战，但此时起义实际上已被镇压，法网正在向他收紧，一支舰队被派去在

sentences.en: him on the Chersonese.
sentences.zh: 切索内斯拦截他。

sentences.en: Um, he manages to escape it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他设法逃脱了。

sentences.en: Um, there's a, a, a, a chase all the way across the Aegean, um, Miltiades manages to, to, to reach Valerum, the harbor of Athens, just in the nick of time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，爱琴海全境都展开了追捕，米提亚德在千钧一发之际设法抵达了雅典的港口法勒隆。

sentences.en: Um, but even when he arrives in Athens, his troubles aren't over because of course he is an aristocrat and he had been himself, uh, a tyrannos, uh, a strong man.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但即使他抵达雅典，麻烦也并没有结束，因为他毕竟是一个贵族，而且他自己也曾是一个暴君、一个独裁者。

sentences.en: And so he's viewed with a good deal of suspicion in Athens.
sentences.zh: 所以在雅典，人们对他的戒备心很重。

sentences.en: And in fact, later that year, he is prosecuted for his tyranny in the Chersonese.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在那年晚些时候，他因在切索内斯的暴政而遭到起诉。

sentences.en: Um, however, he is acquitted, but not only is he acquitted, but he's elected to the board
sentences.zh: 不过，他被宣告无罪了，不仅如此，他还当选为

sentences.en: of the 10 generals whose role it is, um, in this democracy to provide advice and support to the
sentences.zh: 十将军委员会的成员，在这个民主制国家中，他们的职责是为

sentences.en: Athenian Supreme Commander, who's called the War Archon and who again is kind of elected for, uh, an annual term.
sentences.zh: 雅典最高指挥官（被称为执政官，也是按年选举产生）提供建议和支持。

sentences.en: Um, and the reason for this, I think is because people in Athens are aware that the Persian shadow is lengthening and that Miltiades is their city's most seasoned Persian fighter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为原因在于雅典人意识到波斯的阴影正在逼近，而米提亚德是他们城邦中最经验丰富的抗波斗士。

sentences.en: And although nobody really likes him, they think this is a guy who knows what he's talking about.
sentences.zh: 尽管没多少人真正喜欢他，但他们觉得这家伙是个内行。

sentences.en: I mean, we should listen to what he's saying.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们应该听听他的意见。

sentences.en: And so I think Miltiades' election as one of these 10 generals serves as a signal to everyone to would-be appeasers in Athens, to other Greek cities and to the Persians that
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为米提亚德当选为十将军之一，向雅典的所有绥靖主义者、其他希腊城邦以及波斯人发出一个信号：

sentences.en: the Athenians, if the Persians attack them are going to fight, they're not just going to submit.
sentences.zh: 如果波斯人进攻，雅典人会战斗到底，绝不仅仅是俯首称臣。

sentences.en: And this is an important signal because back in Persia, the gaze of the great King is now turning on the lands of the barbarous far WeSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的信号，因为在波斯，大王的目光现在正转向遥远蛮荒的西方土地。

sentences.en: Now, why though?
sentences.zh: 那么，这又是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Because my sense of this has always been that the Persians are so rich, so powerful, so important.
sentences.zh: 因为我对此的看法一直是，波斯人是如此富有、强大、举足轻重。

sentences.en: Um, and, and, and Athens is just, uh, you know, it's a, uh, to, to the Persian sensibility, what is it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且雅典只是，你知道的，在波斯人看来，这算什么？

sentences.en: It's a rogue state, a terrorist state that is way out there on the fringe.
sentences.zh: 它不过是一个偏居边缘的流氓国家、恐怖主义国家。

sentences.en: I suppose you might say, why bother?
sentences.zh: 我想你可能会说，何必去管它呢？

sentences.en: But then on the other hand, why not?
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，为什么不管呢？

sentences.en: If it's only, if it's a little rogue state, why not punish it?
sentences.zh: 既然它只是个小小的流氓国家，为什么不惩罚它一下？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you got to lose?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有什么好损失的？

sentences.en: Well, I think the Persians think there are good geopolitical reasons for it, because if the punishment of Athens is delayed, then it risks encouraging the emergence of
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为波斯人觉得这样做有充分的地缘政治理由，因为如果对雅典的惩罚被推迟，就会冒险助长

sentences.en: other similar terrorist states in the mountainous wilds of Greece.
sentences.zh: 希腊山地荒野中其他类似恐怖主义国家的涌现。

sentences.en: I think Greece to the Persians is what Afghanistan was to the Americans in the wake of 9-11.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于波斯人来说，希腊就像911事件之后的阿富汗对于美国人一样。

sentences.en: You know, you, we need to go and stamp this nonsense out.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们需要去把这种荒唐行径彻底铲除。

sentences.en: But there is also this cosmic dimension, which I think Darius takes very seriously, that he's
sentences.zh: 但还有一个宇宙层面的维度，大流士对此非常重视，那就是阿胡拉·马兹达

sentences.en: been given the rule of the world by Ahura Mazda, and Athens is patently a stronghold of the lie,
sentences.zh: 将世界的统治权交给了他，而雅典显然是谎言的据点，

sentences.en: and that, um, you know, this, that they're worshipping Deiva's demons there, and it needs to be purged with fire.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，你知道的，他们在那里崇拜“得伐”（恶魔），必须用烈火将其净化。

sentences.en: You know, the Persians need to get in there and, uh, restore truth and order.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，波斯人需要攻进去，恢复真理和秩序。

sentences.en: Um, and you can see that, that, that those two notions, the geopolitical and the kind of,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可以看到，这两种观念，即地缘政治的观念和那种

sentences.en: the religious, if you want to put it like that, I mean, they coalesce very readily, uh, they
sentences.zh: 宗教的观念（如果你愿意这么说的话），它们很容易融合在一起，

sentences.en: coalesce in the 5th century BC, as they have coalesced many, many times in subsequent history.
sentences.zh: 它们在公元前5世纪融合了，就像在后来的历史中无数次融合过那样。

sentences.en: And also, of course, if they capture Athens, it's, it then provides a base, perhaps for the
sentences.zh: 当然，如果他们占领了雅典，这也可能为

sentences.en: conquest of the rest of mainland Greece, all of which means that the storm clouds of war are starting to gather over the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 征服希腊本土的其余部分提供一个基地，所有这些都意味着战争的暴风雨开始在爱琴海上方聚集。

sentences.en: And Darius's policy is, um, is twofold.
sentences.zh: 大流士的政策是双重的。

sentences.en: Firstly, he wants to complete the conquest of the land approaches to Greece.
sentences.zh: 首先，他希望完成对通往希腊陆路通道的征服。

sentences.en: So that's from the Hellespont all along the northern Aegean coaSt. And secondly, he wants to intimidate, if he possibly can,
sentences.zh: 也就是从赫勒斯庞特一直延伸到整个北爱琴海海岸。其次，如果可能的话，他希望威慑

sentences.en: the various Greek cities in mainland Greece, um, and receive their submission without actually having to fight them.
sentences.zh: 希腊本土的各个城邦，在不诉诸战争的情况下迫使它们臣服。

sentences.en: So the advance from the Hellespont along the north Aegean coast, he entrusts yet again to, um, a member of his family.
sentences.zh: 因此，从赫勒斯庞特沿北爱琴海海岸推进的任务，他再次委托给了他的一位家庭成员。

sentences.en: This is his son-in-law, um, a guy called
sentences.zh: 这就是他的女婿，一个名叫

sentences.en: Mardonius, who is incredibly dashing, um, perhaps a little bit too dashing.
sentences.zh: 玛尔多尼乌斯的家伙，他极其意气风发，嗯，也许稍微有点太风发了。

sentences.en: Um, but he, he knocks out
sentences.zh: 嗯，但他击溃了

sentences.en: Macedon.
sentences.zh: 马其顿。

sentences.en: So this is the kingdom that in due course will produce Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 这就是日后将诞生亚历山大大帝的那个王国。

sentences.en: But for now, the king of Macedon, who is also called Alexander, he goes, yeah, fine, I'm giving up.
sentences.zh: 但目前，马其顿国王（也叫亚历山大）表示，好吧，我投降。

sentences.en: He presents earth and water to the Persian ambassadors.
sentences.zh: 他向波斯使者献上了土地和清水。

sentences.en: And this means that Persian rule now extends all the way from
sentences.zh: 这意味着波斯人的统治现在从

sentences.en: Hellespont to the foothills of Mount Olympus, the mountain where the gods of the Greeks have their palace.
sentences.zh: 赫勒斯庞特一直延伸到了奥林匹斯山的脚下，那是希腊诸神拥有宫殿的山脉。

sentences.en: There's only two drawbacks to this triumphal approach.
sentences.zh: 这次凯旋的进军只有两个美中不足的地方。

sentences.en: The first is that Mardonius' fleet is shipwrecked off, uh, Mount Athos in the, the north of, of Greece.
sentences.zh: 第一个是玛尔多尼乌斯的舰队在希腊北部的阿索斯山附近遭遇海难。

sentences.en: Um, and Mardonius himself sustains quite a severe wound.
sentences.zh: 嗯，玛尔多尼乌斯本人也受了相当重的伤。

sentences.en: He's kind of gone off on a, a, a dashing expedition against a mountainous tribe and he's ended up with, uh, with a rather severe wound.
sentences.zh: 他当时带兵对一个山地部落进行了一场意气风用的远征，结果受了挺严重的伤。

sentences.en: So that knocks him out of the, uh, of the immediate engagements.
sentences.zh: 这使他无法参与随后的即时战事。

sentences.en: And then the following year after Mardonius has conquered, um, Macedon in 492, in 491, um, the Persian ambassadors are sent to the cities of mainland Greece.
sentences.zh: 而在第二年，即玛尔多尼乌斯于公元前492年征服马其顿之后的公元前491年，波斯使者被派往了希腊本土的各大城邦。

sentences.en: And most of the Greek cities do submit.
sentences.zh: 大多数希腊城邦确实屈服了。

sentences.en: They do offer up earth and water.
sentences.zh: 它们确实献出了土地和清水。

sentences.en: I guess they feel we've got nothing to lose.
sentences.zh: 我想它们觉得我们没有什么可失去的。

sentences.en: I mean, we might as well play it safe, but there are other cities who don't.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们不如稳妥行事，但也有其他城邦没有这样做。

sentences.en: And there are two in particular who pointedly reject the Persian demand for submission.
sentences.zh: 特别是其中有两个城邦断然拒绝了波斯人要求臣服的要求。

sentences.en: And the first of course is Athens.
sentences.zh: 当然，第一个是雅典。

sentences.en: And here, um, not only are the demands of the great King dismissed, but his ambassadors are tried, convicted and put to death.
sentences.zh: 在这里，大王的无理要求不仅被断然拒绝，他的使者还被审判、定罪并处以死刑。

sentences.en: And the man who instigates this legal process is Miltiades.
sentences.zh: 发起这一法律程序的人正是米提亚德。

sentences.en: And the result of course, is to ensure there is no way back now for Athens.
sentences.zh: 当然，这样做的结果是彻底断绝了雅典人的退路。

sentences.en: It's fight or perish, you know, there is no other option.
sentences.zh: 要么战斗，要么灭亡，你知道的，别无选择。

sentences.en: The second city that refuses to offer earth and water to the
sentences.zh: 第二个拒绝向波斯使者提供土地和清水的城邦

sentences.en: Persian ambassadors is Sparta, the most formidable military power in Greece.
sentences.zh: 是斯巴达，希腊最强大的军事力量。

sentences.en: And so she cannot afford to lose face.
sentences.zh: 因此它绝对不能丢面子。

sentences.en: It's very important to the maintenance of her prestige and of her kind of, um, empire in
sentences.zh: 为了维系它的威望以及它在伯罗奔尼撒（希腊南部）的霸权，

sentences.en: the Peloponnese, Southern Greece, that she isn't seen to submit to the demands of some distant foreigner.
sentences.zh: 不向某个远方外国的要求低头，这至关重要。

sentences.en: And the Spartans don't even bother to put the Persian ambassadors on trial.
sentences.zh: 斯巴达人甚至懒得对波斯使者进行审判。

sentences.en: Instead, they fling them down a well and tell them before they drown and I quote Herodotus, if they wanted earth and water, they could find it there.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们把使者扔进了一口井里，并引用希罗多德的话告诉他们在淹死之前：如果他们想要土地和水，就在那里找吧。

sentences.en: And anyone who's seen the film 300, this is the moment where, um, the Persians get kicked down the well and the King shouts out, this is Sparta.
sentences.zh: 任何看过电影《300勇士》的人都会知道，这就是波斯人被踹下井，国王大喊“这就是斯巴达”的时刻。

sentences.en: So two cities are standing against the Persians and these are Athens and Sparta.
sentences.zh: 因此，有两座城邦挺身而出对抗波斯，它们就是雅典和斯巴达。

sentences.en: And it is pretty clear now to everybody in Greece, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 现在希腊的每个人都看得相当清楚了，对吧？

sentences.en: That the Persians are, they're not going to, you know, take this line down.
sentences.zh: 波斯人是绝不会就此罢休的。

sentences.en: They're bound to come.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定会卷土重来。

sentences.en: And sure enough, the next year Darius says, let's go for this.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，第二年大流士说，动手吧。

sentences.en: You know, we're going to punish these rogue states.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们要惩罚这些流氓国家。

sentences.en: We're going to impose, we're going to reimpose the law of heaven, order, harmony, stability.
sentences.zh: 我们要重新强加天国的律法、秩序、和谐与稳定。

sentences.en: You know, we are on the side of, we're fighting this axis of evil, which are these current terrorist states.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们站在正义一边，我们正在打击由这些现今恐怖主义国家构成的邪恶轴心。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we will get loads of slaves and looted treasure as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还能顺便捞到无数的奴隶和战利品。

sentences.en: So it's all brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: Everyone's a winner.
sentences.zh: 皆大欢喜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So a huge army, uh, powerful and well equipped, uh, Herodotus says, perhaps 25,000 men leaves Persia in the early months of 490 and they're heading for the distant WeSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，一支庞大、强大且装备精良的军队（希罗多德称大约有2万5千人）在公元前490年的头几个月离开波斯，直奔遥远的西方。

sentences.en: And by the summer they have passed through the Syrian gates and they come down into the plain of Silesia, which is in the, um, southeastern corner of what's now Turkey.
sentences.zh: 到了夏天，他们穿过了叙利亚门，来到了位于现今土耳其东南角的奇里乞亚平原。

sentences.en: And there they find waiting for them a great fleet of ships.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他们发现了一支庞大的船队正在等待着他们。

sentences.en: Some are built as weapons of war.
sentences.zh: 有些是作为战争武器建造的。

sentences.en: Some are there to serve as transport ships and horse transports.
sentences.zh: 有些则是作为运输船和运马船使用的。

sentences.en: The troops and horses board these ships.
sentences.zh: 部队和战马登上了这些船只。

sentences.en: The fleet glides along the Southern coast of Anatolia and then out into the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 船队沿着安纳托利亚南部海岸滑行，然后驶入爱琴海。

sentences.en: And it's under the command of two generals.
sentences.zh: 这支舰队由两位将军指挥。

sentences.en: And one of these is a Persian inevitably called Artafernes.
sentences.zh: 其中一人毫无疑问是一位名叫阿塔费尔内斯的波斯人。

sentences.en: It's always so confusing ancient history.
sentences.zh: 古代历史总是这么容易让人混淆。

sentences.en: Um, and he is the son and the namesake of the governor of Sardis.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是萨底斯总督的儿子，并且和总督同名。

sentences.en: And so therefore he is the nephew of Darius.
sentences.zh: 因此，他是大流士的侄子。

sentences.en: Um, he's quite young.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他相当年轻。

sentences.en: The effective commander, um, is a mead called Datis.
sentences.zh: 实际上的指挥官是一个名叫达蒂斯的米底人。

sentences.en: He's been given the commission because he's a very seasoned Greek fighter.
sentences.zh: 他被委以重任，因为他是一位经验丰富的抗希腊斗士。

sentences.en: He's a veteran of the Ionian revolt, but he also has a good understanding of the Greeks.
sentences.zh: 他是伊奥尼亚起义的老兵，对希腊人也有很好的了解。

sentences.en: He respects their gods.
sentences.zh: 他尊重他们的神灵。

sentences.en: He even to a degree speaks their language, which is kind of very unusual among the Persians.
sentences.zh: 他甚至在某种程度上会说他们的语言，这在波斯人中相当罕见。

sentences.en: And Datis has been given very precise orders by, uh, by the King of Kings.
sentences.zh: 万王之王向达蒂斯下达了非常具体的命令。

sentences.en: He's to conquer Naxos.
sentences.zh: 他要征服纳克索斯。

sentences.en: So the island that Aristagoras had been defeated by and all the other islands of the Aegean.
sentences.zh: 也就是那个曾让阿里斯托格拉图斯铩羽而归的岛屿，以及爱琴海的所有其他岛屿。

sentences.en: And then he is to, um, land in mainland Greece and he is to reduce Athens and Eretria to slavery and bring the slaves before the King.
sentences.zh: 然后他要登陆希腊本土，将雅典和埃雷特里亚沦为奴隶，并将这些奴隶带到国王面前。

sentences.en: And he proves himself the perfect man for the job.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他是完成这项任务的绝佳人选。

sentences.en: He knows how to storm
sentences.zh: 他懂得如何攻克

sentences.en: Greek cities.
sentences.zh: 希腊城邦。

sentences.en: He lands at Naxos, uh, you know, to take an Aristagoras four months.
sentences.zh: 他在纳克索斯登陆，你知道的，阿里斯托格拉图斯花了四个月时间

sentences.en: And even then he hadn't been able to capture the city.
sentences.zh: 也没能攻占这座城市。

sentences.en: Datis takes the city within a few days.
sentences.zh: 达蒂斯在几天内就攻占了这座城市。

sentences.en: He sacks it, he, uh, loots it, and he rounds up the inhabitants, puts them on the transport ships.
sentences.zh: 他洗劫了这座城市，掠夺了财物，把居民赶集结起来，送上了运输船。

sentences.en: They are going to be taken off as slaves back to the Persian empire.
sentences.zh: 他们将被当作奴隶带回波斯帝国。

sentences.en: But he also knows how to win hearts and minds.
sentences.zh: 但他同样懂得如何赢得人心。

sentences.en: So very near to, um, to Naxos is the island of Delos, which the Greeks think is the birthplace of,
sentences.zh: 所以在离纳克索斯非常近的地方，是提洛岛，希腊人认为那是阿波罗和阿耳忒弥斯的诞生地，

sentences.en: of Apollo and Artemis, you know, Apollo, the radiant God of light and, um, Datis burns enormous amounts of incense before the altar of Apollo.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，阿波罗是光芒四射的光明之神，达蒂斯在阿波罗的祭坛前焚烧了大量的香。

sentences.en: And so you have the two great twin plumes of smoke, one from the burning rubble of Naxos, one from the altar of, um, Apollo.
sentences.zh: 于是你看到了两股巨大的冲天浓烟，一股来自纳克索斯的燃烧废墟，一股来自阿波罗的祭坛。

sentences.en: And it sums up Persian policy to intimidate and to woo, to crush down rebellion, but to offer rewards to those who submit.
sentences.zh: 这就总结了波斯的政策：恩威并施，既要镇压叛乱，又要向顺从者提供奖赏。

sentences.en: Then it is onward to mainland Greece.
sentences.zh: 接着便是继续前进前往希腊本土。

sentences.en: And by late July, the Persian armada is coming within sight of
sentences.zh: 到七月下旬，波斯舰队已经进入了

sentences.en: Attica.
sentences.zh: 阿提卡

sentences.en: And Attica is the region that Athens controls.
sentences.zh: 的视野。阿提卡就是雅典控制的地区。

sentences.en: However, the Persian generals have decided that Athens is going to wait.
sentences.zh: 然而，波斯将领们决定让雅典再等等。

sentences.en: And instead their fleet sails up the narrow straits that separate
sentences.zh: 相反，他们的舰队驶入了狭窄的海峡，

sentences.en: Northern Attica from the island of Yabea, on which Eretria stands.
sentences.zh: 这道海峡将阿提卡北部与埃雷特里亚所在的优卑亚岛隔开。

sentences.en: They sail up about 30, 40 miles.
sentences.zh: 他们向上航行了大约30到40英里。

sentences.en: Um, and there ahead of them is the less formidable of these two cities of the lie, Eretria itself.

sentences.en: And with the flames of the city kind of rising into the sky, the Persian fleet pulls back out and starts to glide back down the straits towards Attica.

sentences.en: So they have the coast of Northern Attica now on their right-hand side as they're sailing back towards the Aegean.

sentences.en: It's got a long, long open beach, which is perfect for drawing ships up onto, you know, they can basically be parked there.

sentences.en: And beyond it, there is a flat level plain, which of course is ideal for the operation of the
